commits.pr_title: [Model] Qwen4Exp: fp8_e4m3 main KV cache on the QSA path
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Let Qwen3.8-Flash-Next store the main K/V cache of its QSA (sparse attention) layers in
`fp8_e4m3` (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`), which is currently rejected on this model. The side
caches of the QSA indexer (raw-key ring and compressed keys) stay in bf16, as does the GDN state.

Scope is deliberately fp8-only (the smallest change that halves the per-token KV footprint),
as suggested in the discussion on #54846; nvfp4 can follow separately. #54846 itself predates the
current QSA kernels (#54513, #54873, #54915 changed `ops/qsa.py` substantially), so this is a
rewrite on top of them rather than a rebase. Related: #54890 (indexer fp8).

## Duplicate check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "qwen4_exp fp8 kv"` / `"QSA kv cache fp8"`:
the open PR in this area is #54846 (fp8 *and* nvfp4 KV on the QSA path). It has been `needs-rebase`
since the QSA kernel changes of #54513 / #54873 / #54915 (644 lines changed in `ops/qsa.py` since its
base), has had no update since the request in its thread to scope it down to fp8 first, and cannot be
applied to current main. This PR is that fp8-only scope, written against the current kernels: it does
not touch nvfp4, so #54846 can still follow for the nvfp4 part. #54890 (indexer cache fp8) is
complementary: this PR leaves the indexer side caches in bf16.

## Changes

- `ops/qsa.py`: the split-K sparse paged attention kernel gets an `IS_FP8` path that loads the
  fp8 K/V pages and applies the per-tensor K/V scales; wrapper and warm-up pass the scale pointers.
- `nvidia/qsa.py`: the backend advertises `supports_kv_cache_dtype` for fp8, the impl accepts a
  `uint8` cache view, the layer binds the fp8 cache and the scales.
- `common/qsa_cache.py`: the side caches accept the cache dtype as a string (they remain bf16).
- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`: a shared problem builder and a new
  `test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_fp8_kv` (scales 1/1 and 0.5/2 against the bf16 reference);
  the existing bf16 correctness test is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "sparse_paged_attention"` on an
  RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120).
- End to end on the same GPU (TP=1, PLE CPU offload from #53899 rebased on this base, 262K
  context, vision on, prefix caching on, no MTP): pool size, needle-in-a-haystack at 125K,
  prefill/decode speed, per-position prompt-logprob trace bf16 vs fp8 (as requested in #54426).

Commands: `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "sparse_paged_attention"` (RTX PRO 6000,
14 passed), `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files, then the serving runs below
(all with PLE CPU offload from #53899 applied on the same base, TP=1).

## Test Result

- Kernel tests: 14 passed (fp8 and bf16 cases).
- KV pool at `--max-model-len 262144`, util 0.91: **434,886 tokens (bf16) → 771,704 (fp8)**, ×1.77.
- Needle at ~125K: 3/3 (three depths). Prefill 11,000 (bf16) vs 11,200 tok/s (fp8); decode
  unchanged (200 tokens in 3.6 s both).
- Per-position prompt-logprob trace on this base (same build, `prompt_logprobs=1`, T=0), fp8 vs
  bf16 compared against the bf16-vs-bf16 run-to-run noise of the same build:

  | prompt | positions | bf16 B − bf16 A (noise) σ / >1 nat | fp8 − bf16 A σ / >1 nat |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | aggregation, 150K | 113,354 | 0.155 / 0.35% | 0.170 / 0.37% |
  | natural text, 8.8K | 8,804 | 0.381 / 3.06% | 0.376 / 2.77% |
  | needle, 125K | 124,933 | 0.016 / 0.00% | 0.015 / 0.01% |

  No drift with position (mean |Δ| per decile flat after the first decile). Greedy outputs differ
  run to run on this model even in bf16 (#54521), so md5 comparisons are not meaningful.
- Needle-in-a-haystack with YaRN ×4 at `--max-model-len 791104`: 12/12 up to 768,938 tokens
  (fp8 KV; the bf16 pool cannot hold that length on one GPU).

Analysis, scripts and text prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic); results run and
reviewed by me.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][PCP] Handle missing DP metadata in one-sided EP
commits.pr_body:
Fix FlashInfer NVLink one-sided expert parallelism when running with `DP=1`.

With DP=1, `ForwardContext.dp_metadata` may be None. The one-sided EP path currently asserts that it exists, causing initialization or execution to fail.

This PR:
- Returns `None` when DP metadata is unavailable.
- Uses the caller’s existing fallback to the local token count, `a1.shape[0]`.
- Preserves the existing behavior for `DP>1.`
- Adds tests for both missing and available DP metadata.

This was encountered with `TP=1, PCP=4, EP`, where expert parallelism is enabled without data parallelism.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Do not classify a stateless first chunk as a decode
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Related to #51039.

A request being forwarded for the first time owns no KDA state, but the non-spec branch of the
Kimi-K3 KDA metadata builder classified any one-token row as a decode
(`split_decodes_and_prefills(m, decode_threshold=1)` with the default
`treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`, `nvidia/kda_metadata.py:405`). When every row in a batch is one
token, `num_prefills` is 0, `has_initial_state` is never computed, and `kda.py` takes the
pure-decode route, which reads `conv_state[slot]` and `recurrent_state[slot]` unconditionally.
`gather_initial_states` is the only thing that masks a stateless slot, and it lives on the
prefill route. Mamba blocks are not zeroed on reallocation
(`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:86` restricts zero-on-allocate to the attention specs), so
such a request silently continues whatever KDA state the previous owner of its recycled block
left behind.

This builder already applies the correct rule on its spec path
(`nvidia/kda_metadata.py:439-447`, "Query length alone cannot distinguish a true decode from a
one-token prefill chunk"), and the Mamba2 builder does the same at `mamba_attn.py:459-481`
("First-token prefills have no prior Mamba state and must stay prefills").

Reachable on stock flags: a one-token prompt scheduled alongside ordinary decodes. Also
reachable when a request's first chunk is clipped to one token by the remaining token budget
(`scheduler.py:990`). Under the default `mamba_cache_mode="align"`,
`Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` often clips that chunk to zero and drops the request from
the step instead. Two cases get through: a block-aligned chunk when the mamba spec carries
prefill checkpoint blocks and no Eagle drafter is configured, which is how Kimi-K3 runs under
the FlashKDA prefill backend (`nvidia/kda.py:598`), and any chunk when the mamba block size
exceeds the prefill budget (`scheduler.py:419-436`). A batch containing any row longer than one
token is unaffected, since `nvidia/kda.py:824` then routes everything through the packed prefill
with the correct `has_initial_state`.

**Three changes:**

1. Classify by state rather than by query length. `no_prior_state` is computed from
   `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound <= query_lens_cpu`, which identifies rows with no computed tokens
   (the bound is documented as precise for prefill rows and optimistic only for async spec
   decode rows, `backend.py:422-426`; an optimistic bound can only miss a stateless row, never
   promote a real decode), and it is additionally masked with the runner's `is_prefilling` flag.
   The dummy batch used for cudagraph capture also has `seq_len == query_len` for every row,
   and without that mask the captured decode graph would record the prefill kernels.

   One-token chunks that resume a partially prefilled request own valid state and keep the
   decode path, so `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False` alone would be wrong: it would move a
   whole decode batch onto `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` whenever a chunked prefill ends on a
   one-token chunk.

2. Re-key the cudagraph staging guard. Decode-graph dispatch is shape based
   (`_is_uniform_decode` decides from token counts before `build()` runs), so a one-token batch
   can replay the captured decode graph even when a stateless first chunk makes it a prefill batch. Keyed on
   `num_prefills == 0` the guard would go false, staging would be skipped, and the replay would
   read state indices staged in an earlier step. The new condition is the one the dispatcher
   uses. On base this is a strict no-op: `num_prefills == 0` and `max_query_len <= 1` are
   equivalent there, and the removed `fill_(NULL_BLOCK_ID)` is dead because entering the guard
   implied `num_decodes == batch_size` (NULL padding still comes from the runner's block table).

3. Exclude cudagraph padding from `num_prefills`. `split_decodes_and_prefills` returns
   `num_reqs - num_decodes`, the whole suffix after the first prefill, so trailing zero-length
   padding rows are counted as prefill requests once a stateless first chunk promotes a row ahead
   of them. The value is only ever compared against zero downstream and never crosses zero, so no
   routing decision changes. `num_prefill_tokens` is inflated separately, since it inherits
   `num_actual_tokens`, which a full cudagraph pads past the last real token; it is recomputed
   from the same real query boundary, and nothing on the KDA execution path reads it. The shared GDN
   builder has all three defects, and #51565 makes the same changes there.

Note on blast radius: `kda.py` does not split the non-spec group, so once `num_prefills > 0` the
whole non-spec batch takes the prefill route for that step. A single freshly admitted request
therefore moves an otherwise all-decode batch off `ops.fused_kda_decode` in eager, `PIECEWISE`,
and uncaptured sizes. Both prefill backends handle all-length-1 `cu_seqlens` correctly.

**What this does not do.** It corrects the metadata, not the dispatch. With the default
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` an all-one-token batch is still dispatched to the captured decode graph on
shape alone, so a replayed graph is unchanged; Mamba2 has the same residual gap. Closing it needs
either worker-side zeroing of mamba pages on reallocation or making the dispatcher decline the
full graph when a mamba group has a stateless row, both core-runner scope, and I am happy to
follow up on either.

It is also a no-op on batches whose metadata carries no `is_prefilling` flag, which is the
microbatching and context-parallel path (`ubatch_utils._make_metadata_with_slice`,
`cp_utils.py`): without the flag the builder cannot tell a first chunk from a resumed one-token
chunk, so it conservatively keeps the base classification there rather than promote a
capture-shaped batch by mistake.

On #51039 specifically: this is a correctness bug that needs no NaN, and it is also one way a
poisoned state block can be inherited by a brand-new request. It does not explain the origin of
the first NaN at 240K, so I am not claiming it resolves that incident.

Coordination: #50855 (draft) touches the same two files and adds an `all_initial_states_fresh`
flag computed from the same fresh-versus-resumed distinction this changes. Whoever lands second should re-check that flag against the new classification.

Line references above are against `d9fbe526c`, main at the time of writing.

## Test Plan

Ten tests in `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`, driving the real builder:

- `test_one_token_first_chunk_is_not_a_decode`: `seq_lens=[100, 50, 1]`, all query lengths 1,
  expects 2 decodes, 1 prefill, `has_initial_state == [True, True, False]`.
- `test_one_token_extend_chunk_stays_a_decode`: `seq_lens=[100, 50, 65]`, all query lengths 1,
  expects 3 decodes and no prefill, so the change cannot regress mid-prefill one-token chunks.
- `test_zero_length_padding_row_is_not_a_prefill`: a padded row is never promoted.
- `test_one_token_first_chunk_excludes_trailing_padding`: two real rows (an ordinary decode,
  then a stateless first chunk) followed by two zero-length padding rows, expects 1 decode and
  1 prefill, 1 token each.
- `test_one_token_first_chunk_excludes_padded_tokens`: the same batch with `num_actual_tokens`
  forced to 4, expects 2 decodes, 1 prefill, 1 prefill token.
- `test_cudagraph_capture_batch_stays_decode_only`: drives `build_for_cudagraph_capture` on a
  uniform dummy batch and asserts it stays decode-only.
- `test_one_token_batch_stages_cudagraph_state_indices`, parametrized over a first-token chunk
  and a pure decode, and `test_all_stateless_one_token_batch_stages_cudagraph_state_indices`
  for the `num_decodes == 0` case: assert the returned tensor is the builder's persistent
  staging buffer and equals `block_table_tensor[:, 0]`.
- `test_multi_token_batch_does_not_stage_cudagraph_state_indices`: a batch with a longer row is
  not a decode-graph batch, so the staging guard must not fire.
- `test_first_chunk_without_prefill_flag_is_left_unclassified`: with no `is_prefilling` flag the
  builder keeps the base classification rather than promote a possibly capture-shaped batch.

## Test Result

- `test_one_token_first_chunk_is_not_a_decode` fails on unpatched main and passes with the
  change.
- Each guard is pinned by mutation. Removing the `is_prefilling` mask fails the capture test;
  keying the staging guard on `num_decodes > 0` fails the all-stateless test; dropping the
  `and m.max_query_len <= 1` clause fails the multi-token staging test; dropping the
  `query_lens > 0` clause fails the zero-length padding test; removing the padding subtraction
  fails the trailing-padding test; dropping the `num_prefill_tokens` recompute fails the
  padded-token test. Making the flag-less fallback a no-op fails the unclassified
  test, and reverting the classification entirely fails three tests.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`: 29 passed.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/` (excluding `test_latent_moe_tail.py`, which needs `ray`, absent in my
  environment): 139 passed, 9 failed, 38 skipped, against 128 passed, 9 failed, 38 skipped on
  the same base (`a3561ef8e`). The difference is the eleven new cases. The nine failures are in
  `test_mla_prefill_context.py` and are present on the unmodified base.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.
- Environment: RTX 5050 (sm_120), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

## Tool assistance

Claude Code was used for the investigation, for reviewing this change, and for drafting this
description. All code was reviewed by me, and every claim above was verified against the tree
and by running the tests reported here.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GDN] Scatter mixed speculative outputs into the caller buffer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mixed speculative/non-speculative Qwen GDN batches currently allocate `merged_out`, scatter both output partitions into it, and copy the complete tensor into `core_attn_out`. This change scatters directly into the caller's buffer, removing one output-sized allocation and the final full-output copy while preserving token order, buffer aliases, and padding rows.

The opportunity was identified while reviewing a submission to a [Pareton AI inference-optimization campaign](https://www.pareton.ai/dashboard/campaigns/7e0462e4-5806-44ac-9f5b-af0542a4bb86). [Pareton AI](https://github.com/Pareton-ai/pareton/blob/main/README.md) evaluates inference patches against pinned vLLM baselines, using reproducible builds and the same sampled workload for contenders within each round. This PR extracts a small, generally applicable improvement from that work for upstream review. Campaign-level results are not presented as measurements of this isolated change.

Co-authored with @xavierlyu and @Danbog32.

### Change

- Write speculative and non-speculative outputs into `core_attn_out` with two `index_copy_` operations along the token dimension.
- Remove the temporary merge allocation and subsequent copy.

Recurrent computation and state updates are unchanged. The optimization applies when speculative and non-speculative outputs coexist; it does not improve paths that bypass this merge. The allocation removed contains `num_actual_tokens × value_heads × value_head_dim` elements.

### Related work

Open-PR searches and diff inspection on September 16, 2026 found no matching change:

- [#57039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57039) reuses FlashInfer prefill output buffers for non-speculative batches; its diff retains the mixed speculative merge changed here.
- [#54612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54612) and [#55260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55260) optimize packed QKV, metadata, and projections without removing this temporary.
- [#50233](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50233) overlaps non-speculative decode/prefill execution; its current diff does not remove the mixed speculative output merge.
- [#50172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50172) and [#55504](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55504) address caching and state recovery rather than this output assembly.

Searches included `GDN scatter`, `GDN stride`, `GDN metadata`, `GDN copy`, `"merged_out"`, and `"GDN" "output" "copy"`.

## Test Plan

Tested September 16, 2026 against vLLM base `0f8fa53acf43a9a6a7a1f7e6b196950c78cd6d7a`, with the production change at commit `5fe281e336f8f25aab2f89cf85c211bf83594551`. The production GDN module in the current PR is byte-for-byte identical to the measured version (SHA-256 `187a368baca93a1d9920d44477c297855413acf7608ace2873ea24b6ff62b21f`). Both serving variants used the wheel built from that exact base. The baseline GDN module matched the repository source byte-for-byte; the patched arm replaced only that module. Native binaries, dependencies, model weights, inputs, and launch settings were identical.

Static hooks ran on macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12.6. The repository tests, GPU component checks, and serving measurements ran on the VM below.

### Test VM and model

| Component | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | 1 × NVIDIA H100 PCIe, 81,559 MiB reported memory, 310 W power limit, MIG disabled |
| CPU / RAM | 20 vCPUs, Intel Xeon Platinum 8352Y @ 2.20 GHz; approximately 125 GiB RAM; container quota 20 CPU cores and 123 GiB memory |
| OS / driver | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.8.0-90-generic, NVIDIA driver 580.126.09 |
| Runtime | Python 3.12.3; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA runtime 13.0; Triton 3.7.1; FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 |
| vLLM | 0.29.1rc1.dev194+g0f8fa53ac; V1 model runner; default compilation and full/piecewise CUDA graphs enabled |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`, BF16, TP=1, text-only inputs |
| GDN / speculative decoding | 24 GDN layers, 32 value heads × 128 dimensions; Triton prefill; MTP with 3 speculative tokens |

This model was selected because its GDN and native MTP paths exercise the mixed speculative/non-speculative merge on one H100. This is a separate upstream validation workload, not a reproduction of the original Pareton campaign score.

### Correctness checks

The [validation bundle](https://github.com/tripathiarpan20/vllm/raw/9055cd31883f61361aa80817f86a734301d8368a/gpu-validation.tar.gz) supplies the supplementary harnesses, fixed workload, raw results, and reproduction instructions.

The supplementary real-kernel harness executes the actual baseline and patched `_forward_core` methods with real metadata construction, convolution, and GDN kernels. Its matrix uses two speculative sequences with query length 4 and two non-speculative sequences with lengths 1 and 1/65/257, BF16 activations, BF16/FP32 recurrent states, and contiguous/strided destinations. It is a component test with supplied weights and states, not a full model accuracy benchmark.

The repository tests are reproducible from the checkout with the matching CUDA runtime and test dependencies:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py

pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py
```

### Serving benchmark protocol

A fixed manifest contains **64 requests** in the same order for both variants: 16 at each input/output token pair of **256/64, 768/128, 1,536/192, and 3,072/256**. Prompt token IDs are saved rather than retokenized between runs. Requests use greedy sampling, seed 42, and `ignore_eos=true` to keep output work fixed. The manifest SHA-256 is `6b5f1be99c276edc155ba269973ad3302c5f85706b4e2eb1d76e3b5a7aaa08c1`.

Each sweep submits the manifest in waves of **1, 4, 8, 16, or 32 concurrent requests**, waiting for each wave to finish. These are client batch sizes; vLLM determines internal token batches. There are four independent server sessions in **baseline → patched → patched → baseline** order, with two measured sweeps per session: **four repetitions and 256 requests per variant/batch size**. The client runs on the same VM over loopback. Startup/compilation and a 32-request warmup with 16 output tokens per request are excluded; the prefix cache is reset before each measured repetition/batch-size cell. There is no simultaneous competing GPU benchmark.

TTFT is measured from client request submission to the first token-bearing response. The table reports the **worst per-run p99 across the four repetitions**, calculated over the 64 requests in each run with NumPy's linear percentile interpolation. Throughput is all generated tokens divided by wall-clock time for the complete 64-request sweep, including waiting for each wave; the report gives the median and min–max range of four observations. No failed or slow measured samples are removed.

Both arms use these serving settings with the pinned model snapshot:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  vllm serve /path/to/pinned/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --served-model-name qwen-gdn --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --seed 42 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --gdn-prefill-backend triton --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --generation-config vllm --language-model-only
```

The measured runs additionally enable the development cache-reset/profiling endpoints and configure the Torch profiler; the profiler is inactive throughout timing. A separate untimed eight-request baseline profile captured **336 `index_copy_` calls into `[1, N, 32, 128]` merge tensors: 168 mixed GDN merges across seven scheduler steps and 24 GDN layers**. This confirms that the model workload reaches the branch changed by the PR. Batch 1 is a useful control because one request cannot create a mixed speculative/non-speculative sequence batch.

## Test Result

### Correctness and static checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing fused sigmoid/GDN recurrent-kernel suite | **18 CUDA cases passed** in the recorded H100 run |
| Supplementary real-kernel mixed-batch comparison | **12 passed**, exact baseline/patched output, convolution-state, and recurrent-state equality |
| CUDA graph replay in those 12 component cases | Exact match to eager execution in both variants; padding and unused strided storage preserved |
| Isolated old/new CUDA output-assembly comparison | **12 passed**, covering BF16/FP32, contiguous/strided output, and 32/256/4,096 tokens; graph replay checked |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks on the production GDN file | Passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, default mypy, and repository checks |
| Explicit Python 3.12 mypy, Python compilation, patch whitespace | Passed |

The archived 26-test log also includes eight mocked assembly cases that were removed from this PR during review. They are excluded from the 18-case result above. This PR adds no new tests; the supplementary real-kernel comparisons and model measurements provide the change-specific validation.

### Isolated output-assembly timing

CUDA-event medians, 25 warmup calls and 50 repetitions of 20 merges; BF16 contiguous output with 32 value heads × 128 dimensions. Each row reports one GDN layer's merge. The full matrix also includes FP32 and strided storage. These are component timings, not end-to-end speedups.

| Tokens | Temporary removed | Eager baseline → patched (µs) | CUDA graph baseline → patched (µs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 | 0.25 MiB | 35.05 → 17.95 | 6.59 → 5.33 |
| 256 | 2 MiB | 36.71 → 18.55 | 8.92 → 7.05 |
| 4,096 | 32 MiB | 109.37 → 75.60 | 102.74 → 71.61 |

The 4,096-token case measures a larger tensor than the serving test’s 1,024-token scheduling budget. The direct merge was faster in these isolated measurements; serving results below determine the observed model-level impact.

### Time to first token

All **2,560/2,560 requests succeeded**, generating **409,600 output tokens** across both variants.

Draft acceptance is accepted draft tokens divided by proposed draft tokens, from per-cell Prometheus counter deltas. It is not an accuracy score.

### Compilation and warmup observations

The server logs report the following startup timings. Compilation time is the engine's reported compilation component; JIT kernel warmup is reported separately. These phases are excluded from throughput and TTFT measurements.

| Session, in execution order | Reported compilation (s) | JIT kernel warmup (s) | CUDA graph capture (s) |

Both baseline-a and patched-b loaded cached AOT artifacts for the main and MTP models; patched-a and baseline-b performed a main-model Dynamo/compile pass while reusing the MTP artifact. The first session also incurred substantially more JIT kernel warmup. These observations document startup behavior, but do not establish a compilation-time improvement or regression from the patch. No Triton JIT-compilation warnings occurred during measured serving.

### Generated-output comparison

Every comparison uses the first baseline sweep at the same client batch size as its reference. The following counts require the **entire generated token-ID sequence** to match for a request. Baseline repeats provide a control for run-to-run variation.

The isolated merge is faster and removes the expected temporary allocation. In the serving test, median output throughput changed by **+3.92% at client batch 4** and **+4.10% at batch 8**, while batch 16 was **−1.01%** and batch 32 was **−0.46%**. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Report request-level KV load failures under HMA
commits.pr_body:
Implements my suggestion back in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50388#pullrequestreview-4827494872, reverting PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50388 in doing so.

## Background

#50388 fixed a hard crash (`ValueError: too many values to unpack`) that hit the scheduler whenever a KV load failure was reported on a hybrid (HMA) KV cache layout. The crash happened in `_report_failed_recv` when unpacking multi-group block ID tuples, and the fix taught the scheduler how to unpack them.

The unpacking was never really the problem, though. Under HMA the scheduler tracks a single merged KV cache group while block IDs are only unique *within* a group, so a block-level failure report is ambiguous by construction — there is no correct way for the scheduler to interpret "block N failed" when the same block ID exists in multiple groups. Patching the unpack just moved the ambiguity around.

Nixl ran into the same situation earlier and solved the simple way in #35264: when HMA is required, `_report_failed_recv` skips block-level reporting entirely and the request is reported as a whole via `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving`. The scheduler already handles `failed_recving` for `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests under both the recompute and fail policies, so no scheduler-side changes are needed.

## What this PR does

Reverts #50388 and mirrors the Nixl approach in the two connectors that could still hit the crash:

- **MooncakeConnector (P2P)**: the worker determines `_is_hma_required` the same way its scheduler does, and under HMA routes failed receives to a request-level queue surfaced through a new `get_transfer_results()` on the worker, which the connector delegates to. Requests that failed before any blocks were assigned locally are still aborted as before.
- **MooncakeStoreConnector**: all mooncake store loads are asynchronous, so load failures land on requests in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. The worker passes the HMA flag into `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`, and the three failure sites (oversized key, partial batch, exception) report the request via `failed_recving` instead of invalid block IDs. The worker aggregates these across receive threads.

Non-HMA layouts keep the existing block-level failure reporting unchanged.

## Testing

Added unit tests for both connectors covering the HMA case (failure reported as `failed_recving`, no invalid blocks touched) and the non-HMA case (block-level behavior preserved), alongside the existing mooncake and load-failure-recovery suites.

To be explicit: this reverts #50388 on purpose rather than building on it, because the block-level reporting path it fixes cannot be made correct under HMA — the group information is simply not there at the point of failure. If reviewers feel strongly about keeping the scheduler-side unpack robustness anyway, that could be reintroduced separately, but I'd rather not keep dead ambiguity-handling code around.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Let an optional Literal flag accept the None it advertises
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`_compute_kwargs` makes an optional field's flag accept `None` by wrapping its type, then advertising the sentinel:

```python
if type(None) in type_hints and not contains_type(type_hints, bool):
    kwargs[name]["type"] = optional_type(kwargs[name]["type"])
    if kwargs[name].get("choices"):
        kwargs[name]["choices"].append("None")
```

but `optional_type` returns the **object** `None`, not the string:

```python
def _optional_type(val: str) -> T | None:
    if val == "" or val == "None":
        return None
    return parse_type(return_type)(val)
```

argparse applies `type` **before** it checks `choices`, so the converted value is `None` while the registered choice is `"None"`, and the flag rejects the value its own help text offers:

```
$ vllm serve ... --collect-detailed-traces None
error: argument --collect-detailed-traces: invalid choice: None (choose from 'all', 'model', 'worker', 'None')
```

The message is self-contradictory: it lists `'None'` among the valid choices in the same breath as refusing it. The empty string, the other spelling `optional_type` accepts, fails identically. There is no way to pass these flags the value they document, so the only route to `None` is to omit the flag entirely.

16 flags are affected:

```
--kv-role                       --pooling-type            --profiler
--safetensors-load-strategy     --seq-pooling-type        --proton-backend
--ssu-algorithm                 --tok-pooling-type        --proton-hook
--mm-encoder-attn-dtype         --task                    --proton-output-format
--collect-detailed-traces       --method                  --moe-backend
--kv-cache-dtype
```

## Fix

Append the sentinel that survives the conversion:

```python
kwargs[name]["choices"].append(None)
```

argparse `str()`s choices when it renders help, so `--help` is byte-identical:

```
before:  [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}]
after:   [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}]
```

## Not a duplicate

Searched `argparse_utils`, `load_config_file`, `optional_type`, `choices`, and `"invalid choice"` across open issues and PRs. The nearby open work is on a different defect in a different file: #49057 fixes `false` booleans in YAML configs and #51623 / #52077 handle empty YAML configs, all in `vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py`. This one is in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` and is about CLI choices, and this PR does not touch `argparse_utils.py` at all.

## Tests

`test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli` in `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`, built on the `DummyConfig.optional_literal` fixture that file already defines. It pins both spellings `optional_type` accepts, that a real choice still works, and that `None` is still advertised in help, which is what made the rejection contradictory.

```
                                                 before          after
test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli    FAIL            PASS
                                                 (SystemExit 2)
```

**How it was run.** `python -m pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` exits 139 on this machine, on a clean tree as well as with this change, because collection segfaults inside native `xgrammar` init. That is unrelated to this PR, so the test body was executed standalone against the real `get_kwargs` and the real `DummyConfig` lifted from the file with `ast`, once against unmodified `arg_utils.py` and once with the change. The 16-flag list above was produced the same way, by running `get_kwargs` over every dataclass in `vllm.config` and reporting fields whose choices contain the string `"None"` but not the object; it goes from 16 to 0 with this change.

`ruff check` gains no new findings (the file's 2 pre-existing ones are unchanged) and `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted.

**No model evaluation results.** This changes argument parsing only: nothing about model output, accuracy or serving behaviour moves. The sole behavioural difference is that a value already listed in `--help` is now accepted instead of erroring out, so there is nothing to evaluate.

AI assistance was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Optimize Sarvam MLA routing and preserve FP32 router logits
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix Sarvam MLA's missing flat-routing configuration and preserve the configured router-logit dtype through expert selection. On the tested BF16 B200 setup, these changes enable the supported TRTLLM MoE path and reduce router overhead while removing an unnecessary BF16 narrowing of FP32 logits.

The source diff is confined to `vllm/model_executor/models/sarvam.py`:

- Default absent or `None` `n_group` and `topk_group` to `1`. The model uses flat top-8-of-128 routing (verified). A single group expresses that configuration and allows the supported TRTLLM implementation to be selected. Explicit checkpoint values are preserved.
- Replace `nn.Linear` plus input/output casts with the existing `GateLinear(out_dtype=router_dtype)`. With the default FP32 router output, the tested path uses BF16 inputs/weights and FP32 accumulation/output, and keeps those logits in FP32 for routing. Previously, the FP32 linear result was narrowed to the hidden-state dtype before expert selection. Other configured router output dtypes remain respected.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open upstream PRs for `sarvam`, `sarvam routing`, and `sarvam GateLinear`; no open PR addressing these router changes was found.

## Test Plan

Validation below combines local checks on the merged branch with historical GPU experiments on the constituent changes. **The GPU results predate the latest upstream merge; they are not a fresh evaluation of this merged head.** This is a draft for human review and post-merge validation.

### Performance

Plain Sarvam step-1350 checkpoint, BF16, 2× NVIDIA B200, TP=2, no speculative model. Gate comparisons used EP off, compilation enabled, prefix caching disabled, maximum model length 32,768, and fixed real-data prompts truncated to 8,192 tokens. Each case used five timing repetitions and medians. Decode step time was estimated as `(median time for 136 output tokens − median time for 8 output tokens) / 128`, with EOS ignored. Prefill throughput uses the corresponding timing intercept and includes admission/scheduler overhead.


| Batch | Control decode ms/step | Repeated control | GateLinear decode ms/step | Speedup against both controls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.844 | 4.664 | 4.473 | 1.043–1.083× |
| 32 | 15.806 | 15.747 | 15.304 | 1.029–1.033× |

| Batch | Control prefill tokens/s | Repeated control | GateLinear prefill tokens/s | Speedup against both controls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 62,419 | 62,298 | 67,078 | 1.075–1.077× |
| 32 | 67,655 | 67,035 | 70,294 | 1.039–1.049× |

Separately, the flat-routing defaults switched the tested MoE path from CUTLASS to TRTLLM and measured **1.11–1.17× decode throughput and 1.03–1.04× prefill throughput**.

### Routing precision verification

An isolated router experiment used real gate weights from all 31 MoE layers, synthetic layer-normalization-scaled inputs, 65,536 inputs per layer, and three seeds on B200: **6,094,848 layer/input comparisons**.

| Candidate compared with the old FP32-gate → BF16-logit path | Inputs with a different selected expert set |
| --- | ---: |
| BF16 gate, still narrow logits to BF16 | 630 / 6,094,848 (0.0103%) |
| BF16 gate, retain FP32 logits | 133,833 / 6,094,848 (2.1958%) |
| FP32 gate, retain FP32 logits | 133,842 / 6,094,848 (2.1960%) |

Removing the logit downcast accounts for the dominant change in expert selection. This is intentionally not bit-exact to the old path: rounding logits before sigmoid/bias/top-k can alter close routing decisions. These counts measure expert-set disagreement, not task error rates, and do not establish exact equivalence between the two FP32-output candidates or full training/inference numerical parity.
Separate evals like AIME, GPQA, TAU2, etc were conducted to ensure parity in quality.

### End-to-end repeatability

Each run scored the same **687,500 positions across 200 fixed prompts**, up to 4,096 tokens each, at **concurrency 1**, with 2×B200, TP=2, EP enabled, BF16, compilation enabled, and prefix caching disabled. A disagreement means a different top-1 next token given the same dataset prefix; this is teacher-forced agreement, not diverging free-running generations. Captures contain top-1 token IDs and saved log probabilities, not full logit tensors.

| Historical build | Selected MoE backend | Top-1 differences against its repeat |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Base commit (main) | CUTLASS | 67,408 / 687,500 (9.805%) |
| Flat-routing defaults (`879e62199d`) | TRTLLM | 0; saved log probabilities bit-identical |
| GateLinear / FP32 logits (`647516fb80`) | TRTLLM | 0; saved log probabilities bit-identical |

Each repeat pair shared an allocation; different historical builds ran on different nodes using the dependencies installed at experiment time. The measured repeatability boundary is the flat-routing/backend-selection change. This does not isolate the internal cause of the earlier variance or establish determinism at higher concurrency.

Cross-implementation diagnostics also showed that scale placement and bias handling affect Sarvam-versus-DeepSeek agreement. Those diagnostic modifications are excluded from this PR; DeepSeek agreement is not treated as proof of task accuracy.

## Test Result

Checks run on the merged branch:

```text
uv tool run ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/sarvam.py        PASS
uv tool run ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/sarvam.py  PASS
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD                           PASS
```

AI assistance was used to prepare and review this contribution and summarize the recorded experiments. Human review and final validation remain required.

commits.pr_title: [Model][DSv4.1] FlashMLA mega attention and the NVFP4 compressed KV cache
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #56344, which closed when its base branch `dsv41-optimized` was deleted.

FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel does Q RoPE, sparse attention, the output's inverse RoPE and its FP8 cast in one launch, writing straight into the buffer `wo_a` consumes. It arrives as `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) with its own attention layer, plus the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV record that only this kernel can read — and, as of this revision, **it is the SM100 default** rather than an opt-in backend.

Rebased onto current `main`, which now includes #56441 (KV-only DSpark context insertion); that PR touched the same translation unit and its interaction with this one is described under *Rebase onto #56441* below.

## The interface capability the base layer acts on

`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query` — the attention kernel applies the Q norm and RoPE itself and reads Q in its own chunk-interleaved layout, so the layer's fused KV insert reduces to a zero-pad of Q to the kernel's head count, and to nothing at all once the shard is already that wide.

The output side needs no flag: the mega layer's `_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj` pair speaks `QuantizedActivation` where every other layer speaks bf16 and rotates in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR declared a second capability, `produces_inv_roped_quantized_output`; it had no reader — the dispatch is the override pair — so it is gone.

## Q reaches the kernel through the existing fused op, not a new one

Rather than a separate Triton pad kernel, `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` gains two independent knobs:

- `apply_q_rope` — rotate Q as well; KV is always rotated. A runtime argument, on the `kv_mxfp8` precedent.
- `is_q_interleaved` — read and write Q in the mega layout (32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` per token), which moves the padding heads to the tail of every head-dim chunk. A template parameter, because it selects the address arithmetic.

They are orthogonal, and that is tested. A lane owns dims `[16l, 16l+16)` of its head in **either** layout — only the address differs — so the per-head RMSNorm and the GPT-J RoPE are equally valid interleaved. `test_q_interleaved_is_orthogonal_to_norm_and_rope` pins it over all eight of (16, 64 heads) × (norm on/off) × (RoPE on/off): the head-major result permuted into the interleaved layout must equal the interleaved path on a permuted input, bit for bit, with the KV cache byte-identical so the Q layout cannot leak into the KV half. An earlier revision conflated the two into one flag on the mistaken belief that the layout made RoPE ill-defined; that test fails against the conflated form.

`q_head_padded = 0` additionally asks for the KV insert alone, which is what TP1 wants — its 64 live heads are already the kernel's head count, so no Q pass is scheduled at all.

## One buffer pair per step

The output travels as a `QuantizedActivation` (`kMxfp8Dynamic`: fp8 e4m3 data, packed-ue8m0 MN-major scales). FlashMLA's fused ops take caller-provided `out_fp8` / `out_sf`, so a single buffer pair covers a whole step: the prefill chunks and the decode segment fill disjoint token ranges, and one `fp8_einsum` over all N tokens replaces one call per segment. The scale buffer's head-dim stride is `ceil4(N)` — both what the kernel requires of a caller buffer and what DeepGEMM expects for that N.

`wq_b` rows and `wo_a` columns are permuted once at load into the kernel's chunk-interleaved layouts, so the surrounding GEMMs speak them directly rather than shuffling per step. DSpark's draft layers are ordinary `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s and therefore take the engine-wide backend, so they owe the same post-load permutation; `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` now runs it, where before it finalized only MoE weights and every draft forward hit the layer's own guard.

## NVFP4 compressed cache

`nvfp4_ds_mla` now means the V4.1 MXFP8 sliding-window record beside a 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (256 B of e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims). It rides the byte-width dispatch the fp8 records already use, so `rope_quant_insert` and `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache` pick it up with no call-site change; CuteDSL has no fp4 gather, so that record takes Triton.

This is the format the reference implementation itself stores: `inference/model.py` quantizes the compressed latent with `fp4_act_quant(latent, 16, True, scale_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)` — group 16, e4m3 scales. `fp8_ds_mla` is *more* precise than the reference on that cache, not less.

Each layer declares the packed record its kernel prefers, and an unspecific `--kv-cache-dtype` resolves to it:

| layer | `auto` / `fp8` | explicit `fp8_ds_mla` | explicit `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
|---|---|---|---|
| mega attention | `nvfp4_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | rejected by the backend |
| plain-row (FlashInfer) | `fp8` | — | `ValueError` |

## Default backend on SM100

An unspecified `--attention_config.backend` now resolves to `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` on SM100. The layer answers `is_available_for()` rather than letting the selector guess, because `__init__` raises on topologies the kernel cannot serve — it is SM100 only, it needs `WV_GROUP_SIZE` heads per `wo_a` group, and a build may not carry the kernel at all. On a 64-head model that admits TP1 through TP8 and declines TP16 (4 local heads), which falls through to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` instead of failing at startup.

The default is chosen for TP1's win plus the 45%-smaller compressed record, **not** for a uniform speedup — see the table below, where TP2 through TP8 are a wash. Set `--attention_config.backend=FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` to get the previous path.

## Performance

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`, one GB300, CUDA graphs on, counting every per-step op each path runs (topk_swa=128, topk_extra=512, NVFP4 compressed cache), as mega / `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` microseconds on a 64-head model:

```
  s_q                    1      32     128     256     512
  TP1 (64 live heads)  29/29   31/31   31/40   53/72   96/140    up to 1.45x
  TP2 (32 live)        29/29   31/30   35/35   61/63  110/119
  TP4 (16 live)        29/29   31/29   34/34   59/58  109/109
  TP8 (8 live)         29/29   31/29   33/33   59/57  107/104
```

The decisive variable is live heads over padded heads, not batch size: the kernel absorbs the inverse RoPE and the FP8 cast, whose cost scales with *live* heads, while its own cost scales with *padded* heads — always 64, since FlashMLA's FP8 decode takes only `h_q` in {64, 128}. So TP1 wins and TP2 down cancel to within a few percent. There is no batch size at which falling back pays, so there is no minimum-token threshold and no fallback path to maintain.

An earlier revision of this table also charged the mega arm for a separate Q-pad kernel "that the split-KV path gets for free"; that is no longer true — the pad is now inside the same fused insert both paths run, and at TP1 it is skipped entirely.

These are decode numbers; **prefill is unmeasured**. Measure under CUDA graphs — in eager mode launch overhead swamps both paths and overstates the fused one several-fold.

## Accuracy: measured end to end, with DSpark

The earlier revision listed accuracy as not covered. It now is. Both arms on one GB300, TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at pinned snapshot `517ef625`, identical eval config, DSpark k=5 with **real** rejection sampling (`rejection_sample_method=synthetic` deliberately absent, so acceptance measures the draft rather than echoing the config). The two recipes differ by exactly one engine flag.

| | mega attention (NVFP4) | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (fp8_ds_mla) | history band |
|---|---|---|---|

#56441 added a KV-only context-insert op to the same translation unit. Two of its call sites needed updating for this series and **git reported no conflict on either**, because neither side edited those lines — they would have surfaced only at compile time: `launchFusedDeepseekV4Templated` gains a template parameter (`is_q_interleaved`) and a runtime one (`apply_q_rope`), and the KV-only op calls it. Both are fixed at the call site, with a comment noting that zero query heads means no Q slot is scheduled so neither knob is reachable there.

The two series had also independently arrived at the same `kNumHeadsQPadded == 0` grid fix (I contributed it to #56441 during review); it collapsed to one.


The last two suites are there because the op this PR changes is also called by the **DSv4.0** paths (`deepseek_v4/attention.py`, its dspark, xpu); the two new parameters are defaulted so those call sites still bind, which is worth testing rather than assuming.

New tests cover the NVFP4 record byte-exactly against a reference quantizer derived from FlashMLA's `tests/quant.py` (scales exact, values within half an e2m1 step, untouched rows and page padding preserved), an insert→gather round trip, the `wq_b` / `wo_a` permutations against a reference that permutes the activation instead, the interleaved Q pad (live elements bit-exact, padding heads zero, both grid variants, and the KV-insert-only launch), the norm/RoPE orthogonality described above, and graph-replay coverage that a captured insert refills its allocated Q buffer over changed input.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fall back to CpuPlatform when zentorch fails to import
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52238.

`cpu_platform_plugin()` catches only `ImportError` around `import zentorch`. zentorch is a compiled extension linked against a specific libtorch, so an ABI-mismatched build fails with `OSError: libzentorch.so: undefined symbol: ...`. That escapes the catch, `cpu` never activates, and the user gets `RuntimeError: Failed to infer device type` naming neither zentorch nor the
cause.
#52285 addressed the issue's other half, logging the swallowed plugin exception so the cause is visible under `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`. This is the behavioural half, since the server still refuses to start.

Reviewing #52285, @tlrmchlsmth asked that we be explicit about which exceptions are recoverable rather than catching blanket `Exception` here. So this catches `OSError` only the specific documented failure from a torch/zentorch ABI
mismatch and lets anything else propagate as before. "Not installed" stays at debug, being the ordinary case on AMD machines.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -x -v -s tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py
```

`test_broken_zentorch_falls_back_to_cpu_platform` patches `__import__` to raise `OSError` for zentorch with `_is_amd_zen_cpu()` forced true, reproducing the report without needing an ABI-mismatched zentorch on the machine.
`test_zentorch_failure_other_than_oserror_is_not_recovered` raises a `RuntimeError` instead and asserts detection still ends at `UnspecifiedPlatform`, pinning the catch as narrow.

The test #52285 added asserted the pre-fix `UnspecifiedPlatform` result, so it now asserts the fallback; its plugin-logging coverage moves to a new test using a synthetic failing plugin.

## Test Result

8 passed on an AMD EPYC (Turin) host; `pre-commit` clean on both files. 
Before, detection returns `UnspecifiedPlatform` and startup dies; after:

```
WARNING ... AMD Zen CPU detected but zentorch failed to import, falling back to CpuPlatform. This usually means the zentorch build does not match the installed torch version.
WARNING ... OSError: libzentorch.so: undefined symbol: _ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIfLi0EEEPKT_v

>>> RESOLVED PLATFORM: vllm.platforms.cpu.CpuPlatform
```

commits.pr_title: [XPU][Bugfix] Fix Qwen2-Audio ValueError on audio clips longer than 30s
commits.pr_body:
# [Bugfix] Fix Qwen2-Audio ValueError on audio clips longer than 30s

## Purpose

`InputProcessingContext.call_hf_processor()` sets
`merged_kwargs.setdefault("truncation", False)` so the dummy placeholder
text passed to the HF processor isn't cut short — vLLM needs the full
untruncated placeholder sequence to keep multi-modal token positions
aligned with the audio embeddings.

`Qwen2AudioProcessor` forwards that same `truncation` kwarg unmodified to
its Whisper-style feature extractor, whose own default is
`truncation=True`: it truncates/pads every audio clip to the model's
fixed 30s window (3000 mel frames). With `truncation=False` leaking in
from the text-side default, clips longer than 30s are no longer
truncated, so their extracted `input_features` keep their native (larger)
frame count. This later fails `Qwen2AudioFeatureInputs`' fixed-shape
validation:

```
ValueError: input_features dim[2] expected 3000, got 3495
```

which crashes the engine core and takes the whole server down
(`EngineDeadError`).

First introduced by 0b19ebcacd0e9578460206035c4b3575361c19c4
("[MM] Simplify `_apply_hf_processor_main` (#53275)"), which added the
`truncation=False` default in `call_hf_processor()`. Not
`--enforce-eager`-specific — reproduces on both eager and
`torch.compile` paths, since the bug is in multi-modal preprocessing,
before model execution.

## Fix

`Qwen2AudioMultiModalProcessor._preprocess_hf_mm_data()` now explicitly
sets `truncation=True` in the kwargs it returns, so it wins over
`call_hf_processor()`'s `setdefault()`. The dummy-text truncation this
default was originally protecting against is unaffected here — the
dummy text is tiny (`<audio_bos><audio_token><audio_eos>`) and never
actually gets truncated either way.

## Test Plan

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  -cc '{"inductor_compile_config":{"benchmark_combo_kernel":false}}' \
  --port 8001 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":1}'
```

Client (any audio clip longer than 30s triggers it; the snippet below
synthesizes one so it's fully reproducible without external data):

```python
import base64, io, requests, numpy as np, soundfile as sf

sr = 16000
duration_s = 35  # > 30s Whisper window
audio = (0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 440 * np.arange(sr * duration_s) / sr)).astype(np.float32)

buf = io.BytesIO()
sf.write(buf, audio, sr, format="WAV")
b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")

resp = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:8001/v1/chat/completions",
    json={
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct",
        "messages": [{
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Transcribe the audio."},
                {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": b64, "format": "wav"}},
            ],
        }],
        "max_tokens": 64,
    },
)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text[:500])
```

## Test Result

Before fix: server crashes on the first request with a >30s audio clip:
```
ValueError: input_features dim[2] expected 3000, got 3500
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```
All subsequent requests get `500 Internal Server Error`, server has to
be restarted.

After fix: server processes the same request successfully, returns a
transcription with `200 OK`. Confirmed on Intel BMG B70 (XPU) and NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (CUDA).

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Frontend] Expose effective attention block size for DCP
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With decode context parallelism (DCP), a physical KV cache block of 16 tokens can represent 64 tokens across four ranks. Clients need that effective size to interpret full-attention cache events.

This PR exposes the value as `CacheConfig.effective_attention_block_size`, populated from the initialized cache managers. Python clients read it from their config, and the engine startup response carries it to Rust and gRPC `Control.GetServerInfo`.

Existing physical block-size fields remain unchanged. Without DCP, the effective size matches the full-attention physical block size. The new field is optional and unavailable when the engines cannot report a common full-attention block size.

Duplicate checks found no open PR exposing this DCP-adjusted value through config, startup metadata, and gRPC.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
```

calls `configure_root_logger()` at module level, setting all root
handler levels to `ERROR`. When `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` shares the
same handler object between root and `vllm` loggers, this silences
vLLM startup INFO/WARNING logs (e.g. chunked prefill diagnostics).

The fix defers the `sagemaker_standards_bootstrap` import from
module-level into `build_app()` where it is actually called, so the
side effect is avoided unless SageMaker integration is actively used.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/vllm-logging.json \
python - <<'PY'
import logging
from vllm.logger import init_logger
init_logger("vllm.repro")
vllm_logger = logging.getLogger("vllm")
root_logger = logging.getLogger()

import vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server  # noqa: F401

# Both handlers should still be INFO (20), not ERROR (40)
assert vllm_logger.handlers[0].level == 20, \
    f"vllm handler level changed to {vllm_logger.handlers[0].level}"
assert root_logger.handlers[0].level == 20, \
    f"root handler level changed to {root_logger.handlers[0].level}"
print("PASS: handler levels unchanged")
PY
```

Test Result

Before: vllm handlers: [<StreamHandler <stdout> (ERROR)>]
After:  vllm handlers: [<StreamHandler <stdout> (INFO)>]

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] tolerate malformed EXIF metadata during hashing (#56527)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56527

When handling images with malformed or corrupt EXIF segments (for example, an APP1 segment containing an invalid TIFF header), calls to `Image.getexif()` raise exceptions such as `SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'...' not valid)` or Pillow internal parser errors.

While `normalize_image` in `vllm/multimodal/image.py` wraps `ImageOps.exif_transpose` in `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` to gracefully tolerate malformed metadata, `MultiModalHasher.serialize_item` previously called `obj.getexif()` directly without error handling in both the `Image.Image` and `MediaWithBytes` branches (`vllm/multimodal/hasher.py`). Because `SyntaxError` does not inherit from `ValueError`, this uncaught exception causes the API server request to abort with HTTP 500.

This PR introduces a dedicated helper `_get_image_id_bytes()` with safe exception handling:
- Reads the optional `Image.ExifTags.Base.ImageID` UUID tag inside a `try ... except Exception:` block.
- If EXIF parsing or header extraction fails for any reason, gracefully falls back to standard pixel hashing (for `Image.Image`) or `original_bytes` (for `MediaWithBytes`), matching the error tolerance of `normalize_image`.

## Test Plan

Added unit test `test_hash_image_malformed_exif` in `tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py`:
- Constructs a JPEG containing a malformed APP1 EXIF segment with an invalid TIFF header.
- Verifies that `MultiModalHasher.hash_kwargs("blake3", image=image)` produces a valid hash without raising `SyntaxError`.
- Verifies that `MediaWithBytes(image, data)` wrapping the malformed image also serializes and hashes successfully.
- Verified existing `test_hash_image_exif_id` continues to pass and correctly extract valid UUID ImageIDs.

Run tests:
```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py -k "test_hash_image_malformed_exif or test_hash_image_exif_id"
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Track cache recency once per request
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The offloading scheduler re-touched the full cached prefix while a request was decoding. Besides doing repeated work, this made frequency-based policies such as ARC count one request as many accesses. Transfer-pinned LRU blocks also re-entered the evictable set in completion order, which could make an early prefix block the eviction victim and leave an unusable cached suffix.

## Fix

- Remove scheduler-driven cache-policy `touch` calls.
- Record the keys actually loaded or offered for store in `ReqContext`, including their end-token positions.
- Apply one logical head-to-tail cache access in `on_request_finished`, independently of later transfer completion order.
- Keep new ARC entries in T1, count each ready reused entry once per request, and adapt B1/B2 ghost hits once before insertion.
- Treat tiering cascade reads as internal pins rather than additional request accesses. Primary recency is committed when the request finishes; secondary cleanup still waits until no more cascades can be submitted.
- Give LRU a logical recency rank separate from physical pinning, with bounded lazy-heap compaction and atomic batch eviction.
- Merge token positions across hybrid KV groups so tails are evicted before heads globally, not only within each group.

The existing `touch` API remains available for compatibility, and the new policy finalization hook has a default implementation for external policies.

Request access accounting is scoped to keys observed by the offloading manager: ready resident keys passed through `prepare_load()` or `prepare_store()` count once per request. A key that remains purely GPU-local and never reaches the CPU manager does not change CPU recency. New writes, speculative `lookup()` calls, and internal tiering cascade reads are not frequency hits.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)
```

## Test Result

- Related unit tests: `303 passed`
  - CPU manager: `50 passed`
  - Tiering manager: `56 passed`
  - Offloading scheduler: `189 passed`
  - Policy factory: `8 passed`
- Pre-commit, including ruff and mypy for Python 3.10: passed
- GPU E2E (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 64-block CPU LRU cache with 16-block replacement): `1/1 passed`; replay observed 768 cached tokens (expected 768), and generated output matched the baseline.
- GPU environment note: the test used nightly image base `1970f3ed4`; the PR Python changes were overlaid, with the scheduler diff applied to that image base to account for one-day API drift.
- Model evaluation: N/A; this changes CPU-cache eviction bookkeeping only.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][AITER] Skip AITER norm kernels when flattening to 2D would copy
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The AITER norm kernels take 2-D inputs only, so the wrappers in
`vllm/kernels/aiter_ops.py` flatten the leading dims with `Tensor.reshape`:

```python
if x.dim() > 2:
    x_original_shape = x.shape
    x = x.reshape(-1, x_original_shape[-1])
```

`reshape` silently degrades to `.contiguous()` when the flattened shape is not
expressible with the input's strides, injecting a whole-tensor device copy. The
support predicates (`rms_no_var_16bit_only`, `rms_add_no_var_16bit_only`) check
only dtype and `variance_size`, so AITER is still selected in that case — and
the copy costs more than the kernel saves.

Per-head QK norm hits this on every layer: `q`/`k` are last-dim slices of the
fused QKV projection viewed as `(num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim)`, whose
leading dims cannot be merged without a copy. Qwen3-8B at 4096 tokens:

```
q_by_head  shape=(4096, 32, 128)  stride=(6144, 128, 1)  is_contiguous=False
q_by_head.reshape(-1, 128) shares storage: False   # full 4096x4096 bf16 copy
```

This adds `flatten_to_2d_is_free(x)` and requires it in both predicates. When it
returns `False`, `IrOp.dispatch` falls through to the next provider — on ROCm
`native`, i.e. Inductor codegen, which consumes arbitrary strides directly and
fuses the norm into its neighbours. Numerically equivalent; only the copy is
gone. The predicate runs once per graph node during `VllmIRLoweringPass`, not
per forward, so it costs nothing at steady state.

**Scope.** Only a rank > 2 input that is a slice of a larger buffer can be
affected; a contiguous rank-3 tensor flattens for free and still dispatches to
AITER. The dividing line is the norm class, not the model family: the 9 in-tree
files whose QK norms are `GemmaRMSNorm` (gemma, gemma2, gemma3, gemma3_mm,
qwen3_5, qwen3_next, rnj1, step3p5, step3p5_mtp) pass an fp32 weight and already
fail the pre-existing `weight.dtype == x.dtype` check, one condition *before* the
new guard, so their dispatch cannot change in either direction. The ~27 files
that build `RMSNorm(head_dim)` for per-head QK norm (qwen3, qwen3_moe, gemma4,
glm4_moe, exaone4, plamo3, lfm2, lfm2_moe, apertus, afmoe, …) are candidates for
the win.

## Test Plan

New `tests/kernels/ir/test_aiter_norm_dispatch.py` asserts the predicate agrees
with whether `reshape` preserves the storage pointer, over flattenable and
non-flattenable layouts.

End-to-end, on 1x MI355X (gfx950) and 1x MI325X (gfx942), TP=1:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1

vllm bench throughput --model <model> \
  --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
```

Three interleaved base/patched pairs per model with the order alternated per
repeat, so drift and thermal ramp are shared rather than charged to one variant;
deltas are pairwise and the reported figure is the median. Each arm gets its own
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` **and** `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` — `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE`
alone does not stop Inductor's FX graph cache, and a shared cache lets the
patched arm reuse graphs the base arm compiled, erasing the difference being
measured. The change is Python-only, so both arms share the same compiled `.so`.

Kernel level: the per-head QK-norm geometries the dispatch probe actually
observed, x {1024, 2048, 4096, 8192} tokens x {q, k}, bf16, compiled through
`VllmIRLoweringPass` with priority `["aiter", "native"]`. Per-call GPU time from
replaying a captured graph over 4 rotating input buffers (so the copy is not
absorbed by Infinity Cache), refill timed separately and subtracted.

Dispatch probe: instrumented the predicate to log every distinct
`(shape, stride, dtype, verdict)` reaching it, per model, with a cold Inductor
cache so the lowering pass reruns.

## Test Result

New tests pass (8/8). Numerics match `native` within `atol=rtol=2e-2` across
bf16/fp16 and contiguous / per-head-strided shapes.

### End-to-end throughput

| Model | dispatch | MI355X (gfx950) | MI325X (gfx942) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (`qwen3_moe`) | 2/3 rejected | **+5.17 %** | **+6.87 %** |
| lfm2-1.2b (`lfm2`) | 2/3 rejected | **+3.19 %** | **+3.28 %** |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (`gemma4`) | 4/6 rejected | **+2.37 %** | **+2.34 %** |
| Gryphe-Gemma-4-31B-StyleTune (`gemma4`) | 4/6 rejected | **+2.48 %** | — |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (`qwen3_5`) | 0/4 reach the guard | no-op control | — |

Every pair is positive on both architectures, including the reversed-order
pairs. Within-variant spread is 0.06–1.03 % except lfm2-1.2b (2.2 %), whose run
is short enough that scheduler ramp dominates. Qwen3-30B-A3B is the cleanest
signal: +5.17 % against a 0.10–0.21 % spread on gfx950. KV cache size matched to
within 0.01 % between arms on every model.

Qwen3.5-122B-A10B is the control: `Qwen3NextAttention` does apply per-head QK
norm on a fused-QKV slice, so it looks like the exact target pattern, but all 28
predicate calls are rejected on weight dtype and **0** reach the flatten guard.
Same for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 at TP=2 and TP=4 (26/26 and 44/44).

### Kernel level

Sum of best-of-3 x 200 iters over all cases:

| Input layout | `aiter` | `native` | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| gfx950 — per-head slice of fused QKV | 1601.4 us | 814.0 us | **1.97x** |
| gfx950 — contiguous per-head (control) | 1007.5 us | 689.3 us | |
| gfx942 — per-head slice of fused QKV | 2635.7 us | 671.9 us | **3.9x** |
| gfx942 — contiguous per-head (control) | 2061.3 us | 650.8 us | |

Splitting the saving by holding the provider at `aiter` and only making the input
contiguous: the hidden copy this PR removes is **75 %** of the win on gfx950 and
**29 %** on gfx942, the remainder being AITER's norm kernel trailing Inductor
codegen at `head_dim`-wide rows, independent of any copy. `native` is close to
layout-insensitive — the strided slice costs it +18 % on gfx950 and +3.2 % on
gfx942, where `aiter` pays +59 % and +28 % — confirming the patch's load-bearing
assumption that Inductor consumes arbitrary strides without materialising a copy.

On the patched tree all slice cases select `native` (814.0 us, matching the
forced-`native` control) and all contiguous cases still select `aiter`,
confirming the guard moves only the layout it targets.

### Dispatch coverage

| Model | implementation | layouts | rejected |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-14B-FP8 / Qwen3-30B-A3B | `qwen3`, `qwen3_moe` | 3 | **2** |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it / Gryphe-Gemma-4-31B | `gemma4` | 6 | **4** |
| lfm2-1.2b | `lfm2` | 3 | **2** |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | `qwen3_5` | 0 | 0 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | `deepseek_v4`, MLA | 53 | 0 |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | MoE, norms already 2-D | 4 | 0 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | no QK norm | 1 | 0 |

Qwen3-8B rejects exactly the two QK-norm layouts `(s, 32, 128)` and `(s, 8, 128)`,
both `stride=(6144, 128, 1)` — `6144` being the fused QKV row stride. Matching
counts on Qwen3-14B-FP8 show quantization is orthogonal. gemma-4 is a broader
case: 4 of 6 layouts rejected across two distinct QKV geometries, while one of
its accepted layouts is a *contiguous* rank-3 vision-tower activation
(`[1, 2048, 1152]`, stride `[2359296, 1152, 1]`), showing the guard rejects
strided slices specifically rather than rank-3 inputs generally.

Unaffected by structure, measured rather than assumed: DeepSeek-V4-Flash and
MiniMax-M2.7 reach the guard with zero rejections, every input 2-D contiguous.
GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) and Kimi-Linear-48B resolve to MLA
implementations (`deepseek_v32`, `kimi_k3`) whose norms are sized only by
`hidden_size` / `q_lora_rank` / `kv_lora_rank`, so no per-head layout can reach
the guard; Falcon-H1 and Granite-4.0-H likewise define `hidden_size` norms only.

Full per-architecture numbers, harness details and the predicate-level
instrumentation are in the comments below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect Mamba block allocation estimate that prevents request admission
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
It is found for Kimi K3, a long request can be rejected admission when loading prefix cache from external KV storage (e.g., Mooncake) and get stuck in the waiting queue forever, causing entire system to stall. commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Use Murmur3 RNG for Gumbel sampling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Replace the Gumbel sampler's Philox-based uniform generation with a manual Murmur3 x86_32 mixing path keyed by request seed, token position, and vocabulary offset. The goal is to preserve the target sampling distribution while improving RNG resolution and avoiding backend-specific math paths.

Related RFC: #54143.

This is not a duplicate of #47524. That PR keeps Philox and combines more of its output bits to improve uniform resolution; this PR evaluates a different RNG and a backend-independent logarithm path. The existing Philox helpers remain available for rejection sampling.

## Implementation

- Generate fp32 uniforms from the full 32-bit Murmur3 result through two exact 16-bit integer-to-float conversions, avoiding backend-dependent uint32-to-float behavior.
- Generate centered fp64 uniforms from 53 random bits and explicitly keep both endpoints open after fp64 rounding.
- Use a stable degree-8 approximation for `log1p(-u)` in the fp32 winning tail instead of a backend-specific libdevice call.
- Keep draft and target sampling on separate noise streams by salting the token position.
- Add Murmur3 known-answer and fp64 endpoint tests, retain the existing distribution tests, and make output-sensitive API tests deterministic where the RNG stream is not the behavior under test.
- Remove the API-level assumption that parallel completions must randomly finish at different lengths. Staggered child completion is already covered deterministically by the `ParentRequest` unit tests.

The current diff touches the sampler, its GPU tests, and three RNG-sensitive entrypoint tests.

## Compatibility Impact

Seeded non-greedy requests produce a different deterministic token sequence because the random-number stream changes. The intended categorical distribution, public API, logits-cache behavior, greedy path, and kernel launch structure are unchanged.

## Test Plan

- Validate Murmur3 outputs against fixed known answers and verify fp64 uniforms exclude both endpoints.
- Run the existing Gumbel distribution, drafting-stream, and edge-case tests on CUDA and ROCm.
- Run structured-output, reasoning, and parallel-completion entrypoint suites after removing assumptions about a particular seeded random sequence.
- Run repository formatting, lint, type, import, DCO, and policy checks.
- Compare Philox and Murmur3 kernel latency on NVIDIA and Ascend hardware.

## Test Result

- Local commit hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, typos, mypy, SPDX, import, and policy checks.
- Targeted Python 3.12 mypy, `compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed for the final fixes.
- [Buildkite CI #86309](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/86309) reported zero failed selected jobs. The NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI300 basic-correctness lanes passed, as did the selected NVIDIA/AMD entrypoint integration lanes. The aggregate Buildkite status remained open on optional manual gates when this result was recorded.
- Split-16 fp32 reconstruction matched correctly rounded fp32 values for 2,000,000 random uint32 inputs with 0 mismatches.
- Joint RNG checks over `(seed, position, offset)` found no detectable abnormal correlation: token-token Pearson z-scores had mean -0.009, standard deviation 0.998, and maximum absolute z-score 3.90; byte, bit, and serial checks were also within expected statistical noise.
- Sampler-level Monte Carlo tests found no detectable categorical bias after using the full 32-bit source. For vocabulary size 129,280 and 100,000 draws, tail-mass z-scores were -1.18 at logit gap 18 and -1.09 at logit gap 20. The earlier 24-bit path produced -5.89 and -5.16 respectively.
### Model-level serving validation (RTX 5090)

A model-level A/B was run with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (vocab 151,936), Model Runner V2, and seeded non-greedy sampling (`temperature=0.8`, `top_p=0.95`). The exact `gumbel.py` files from base `570735520942` and head `2803c10512dd` were tested in the same fixed runtime (vLLM `0.17.2rc1.dev3682+g426e59f62`, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0).

- Functional smoke: two independent no-prefix-cache runs per revision; every run completed 34/34 HTTP requests. In both head runs, all 16/16 sequential prompt/seed pairs and the seeded `n=4` request reproduced exactly. No empty output, engine error, OOM, or NaN was observed.
- Baseline also reproduced 16/16 sequential prompt/seed pairs, but its seeded `n=4` request was not fully identical in either run.
- Base/head output sequences changed as expected with the RNG stream replacement: only 1/16 first-pass completions matched exactly.
- Serving A/B: 5 runs per revision, 128 requests/run, 256 input + 128 output tokens, concurrency 32, fixed request seed, and `ignore_eos`; 640/640 requests succeeded for each revision.

| Metric (median of 5 run-level values) | Baseline | Murmur3 head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 49.22 | 51.26 | +4.15% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 6,299.86 | 6,561.30 | +4.15% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 71.40 | 75.99 | +6.43% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 4.524 | 4.291 | -5.15% |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 4.527 | 4.311 | -4.79% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 91.21 | 103.83 | +13.84% |

commits.pr_body:
# [Bugfix][KV Offload] Check cgroup memory before SHM allocation

## Purpose

Add a cgroup-memory preflight check for SHM-backed allocations, including
CPU KV offload shared regions. The check reports actionable cgroup memory
context before SHM pages are populated.

## Problem

`/dev/shm` free space and cgroup memory are separate constraints. An
allocation can fit the SHM filesystem while the container has insufficient
cgroup headroom. Populating the pages can then trigger a cgroup OOM kill
without an application-level diagnostic.

## Changes

- Keep the existing `/dev/shm` filesystem capacity check.
- Read cgroup v1 and v2 memory limits, including unlimited and missing-file
  cases.
- Cache the cgroup limit, but read current cgroup usage on every check because
  `memory.current` is dynamic.
- Log a detailed preflight snapshot at debug level when headroom is sufficient
  and at warning level when current headroom is below the requested size.
- Continue allocation after a low-headroom warning because cgroup usage can
  include reclaimable file cache.
- Skip the cgroup check when the limit or current usage cannot be read.
- Pass allocation names through SHM broadcast and CPU KV offload paths so
  diagnostics identify the affected allocation.

This PR is not duplicating #55247. That PR addresses CPU KV-cache auto-sizing
and cgroup clamping for NUMA/non-NUMA memory detection, including its own
end-to-end CI coverage. This PR addresses SHM allocation preflight diagnostics
and CPU KV offload shared-memory sizing. The focused utility tests reuse the
same test-file structure to minimize merge conflicts, while retaining only
the behavior required by this PR.

With multiple MCP tool sessions, both Responses contexts register the same cleanup callback once per session. Each callback visits all called tools. This can send duplicate cleanup requests to an open session and attempt another call on a session that has already closed.
