commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix MLA RoPE fused-kernel tests for TheRock image
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
The `Core Operations Kernels` test group fails on TheRock image (see [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12914/list?sid=01a09eed-c3fc-4155-8ae7-ad55792cdc2c&open=false)). This has been root-caused to the Triton 3.8 upgrade.
Specifically, in the computation of RoPE, we compute terms similar to  `x * cos - y * sin`. In Triton 3.7, the LLVM backend lowers to `FMA_F16(x, cos, MUL_F16(-y, sin))`, which is the same as the HIP reference fused kernel. However, in Triton 3.8, the LLVM backend instead lowers to `FMA_F16(-y, sin, MUL_F16(x, cos))`.
In short, the LLVM backend makes a different choice for which product to pre-round to F16 in the fused multiply-add. This pre-rounding can lead to a 1 ULP difference (wrt the product) compared to a hypothetical reference which does all the arithmetic in FP32 before rounding to F16 once at the end.
Thus, the 2 choices of which product to pre-round can lead to differ by up to 2 ULP wrt `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin))`. The current tolerances do not adequately capture the subtleties in this regime, which is partly why the tolerances for this test have been adjusted at least 3 separate times (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51083, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46409, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32408).

## Purpose
This PR reworks and unifies the tolerances for this test for half-precision dtypes on ROCm.
Specifically, for the non-RoPE portions of the tensors, we compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. For the RoPE portions of the tensors, we now have a 2 part test:

1. Compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. The number of failing elements must not exceed 0.01 (for bf16) or 0.0001 (for fp16) of all elements.
2. For all failing elements, check that they differ from the reference elements by up to 2 ULP wrt the relevant products (e.g. `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin), abs(-x * sin), abs(y * cos))` for non-Neox-style RoPE).

## Test Plan
For ROCm 10:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group on AMD CI [with this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list) applied vs [without this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list).

For ROCm 7.2:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group as part of CI on this PR.

## Test Result
The Core Operations Kernels test group is fixed on ROCm 10, and there are no test regressions on both ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Unreadable `prompt_embeds` payload should be a 400, not a 500
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`prompt_embeds` is a base64 blob the caller writes, and `safe_load_prompt_embeds` already answers **400** for every other way of getting it wrong — wrong rank, wrong `hidden_size`, non-float dtype, a payload that deserializes to something other than a tensor, a body that is not valid base64. A payload `torch.load` cannot read *at all* was the one hole: it came back **500**.

torch has no single error type for that, which is why the existing mapping missed it:

| payload | what `torch.load` raises |
|---|---|
| empty | `EOFError` |
| single byte | `IndexError` |
| random bytes | `UnpicklingError` |
| ascii text | `KeyError` |
| truncated zip | `RuntimeError` |
| zip without a tensor | `RuntimeError` |
| legacy pickle of an int | `RuntimeError` |

None of those is a `ValueError`, so `create_error_response` fell through to its `InternalServerError` branch:

```python
elif isinstance(exc, (ValueError, TypeError, OverflowError)):
    err_type = "BadRequestError"
    status_code = HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST
...
else:
    err_type = "InternalServerError"
    status_code = HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
```

`render_prompt` calls `safe_load_prompt_embeds` with no `try` between it and the route, so the caller gets a 500 for a body they simply got wrong. This needs the server started with `--enable-prompt-embeds`; the guard for that flag is the first thing the function checks and is unchanged.

## Test Plan

Each payload is run through the **real** `safe_load_prompt_embeds` and then through the **real** `create_error_response`, so the assertion is about the status code the entrypoints actually produce, not about the exception class alone.

`tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py` (new):

- `test_unreadable_prompt_embeds_payload_is_a_client_error` — 7 payloads, each must raise `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter="prompt_embeds"` and map to 400.
- `test_the_error_body_stays_bounded` — the same 7 payloads with 100 KB of padding appended; the message must stay under 500 characters.
- `test_a_well_formed_payload_still_loads` — positive control.
- `test_a_payload_that_is_not_base64_is_still_a_client_error` — positive control for the stage that already answered 400.

## Test Result

**On `main` (e473e9036), the same seven payloads:**

```
  200  well-formed 2D tensor (control): loaded (3, 8)
*** 500  empty payload: EOFError
*** 500  random bytes: UnpicklingError
*** 500  ascii text: KeyError
*** 500  truncated zip: RuntimeError
*** 500  valid zip, no tensor: RuntimeError
*** 500  legacy pickle of an int: RuntimeError
*** 500  single byte: IndexError
    400  not base64 at all: Error
```

**With this PR:**

```
  200  well-formed (control): (3, 8)
    400  empty payload: VLLMValidationError
    400  random bytes: VLLMValidationError
    400  ascii text: VLLMValidationError
    400  truncated zip: VLLMValidationError
    400  valid zip, no tensor: VLLMValidationError
    400  legacy pickle of an int: VLLMValidationError
    400  single byte: VLLMValidationError
    400  not base64 at all: Error
```

**Regression proven.** The new test file applied to a `main` worktree: **14 failed, 2 passed** — the 2 that pass are the positive controls, which is the point of including them. All 16 pass here.

**Suites:**

- `tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py` + `test_sparse_tensor_validation.py` + `test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py` → **69 passed**
- Whole `tests/renderers/` → 487 passed with 4 failures, all reproduced identically on `main`: 3 in `test_hf.py` (gated HF repos, no network here) and `test_cohere.py::test_async_cohere_renderer_does_not_block_event_loop` (an event-loop timing test; fails on `main` and on this branch in the same run).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all four files.

## Two things worth flagging for review

**1. The sparse-tensor path changes status code too.** `check_sparse_tensor_invariants_threadsafe()` makes `torch.load` raise `RuntimeError` for a malicious sparse tensor, so that rejection was answering 500 as well. It now answers 400 and keeps torch's own reason:

```
`prompt_embeds` could not be deserialized as a torch tensor:
size is inconsistent with indices: for dim 0, size is 10 but found index 999999
```

The rejection itself is unchanged — same payloads refused at the same point.

**2. That required touching two existing test files.** `test_sparse_tensor_validation.py` (4 assertions) and `test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py` (5 assertions) asserted `(RuntimeError, ValueError)` for the **prompt-embeds loader specifically**; they now accept the client error. The `MediaIO` assertions in the same files are deliberately untouched — `ImageEmbeddingMediaIO` / `AudioEmbeddingMediaIO` still surface torch's `RuntimeError`, and this PR does not change that path.

## Notes

- `torch.OutOfMemoryError` subclasses `RuntimeError` and is a server condition, so it is re-raised before the client-error tuple is consulted.
- torch's reason is truncated to 200 characters rather than echoed whole, because it is built from bytes the caller sent — an unpickler that reports an offending global quotes a name the caller chose.
- Found by fuzzing caller-supplied fields of the OpenAI entrypoints and classifying every exception through `create_error_response`. The same sweep put 120,000 malformed multimodal content parts through `_parse_chat_message_content_mm_part` and found **no** 500-class outcome there, so this PR is scoped to the one place that had them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore MTP-retained sliding-window history
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix native KV offload restoring MTP-retained sliding-window blocks that lookup never checked and the producer may never have stored. Implements the conservative coverage option discussed in #56701.

For example, with a 64-token external hit, SWA block size 16, window 32, and three extra retained tokens, lookup checks chunks 2–3 while allocation also restores chunk 1. If chunk 1 is absent or still being written, `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` asserts after the hit has already been admitted. Hybrid store pruning can itself omit chunk 1.

Include `extra_retained_tokens` in aligned/partial lookup coverage, the existing in-flight-load check, and producer store reachability. Preserve the base coverage lower bound so retaining one extra token does not unnecessarily request another chunk. The store mask uses a temporary coverage spec; actual attention windows, allocation, cache keys, and transfer ownership are unchanged. Restoring the required older blocks can increase CPU cache usage and transfer volume.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-13 found no open PR for `56701 in:body` or `extra_retained_tokens offload`. #55818 handles allocation scaling and #53499 page-size normalization; neither fixes this lookup/store mismatch.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing scheduler tests to cover retained history at aligned and unaligned hybrid boundaries, EAGLE tail handling, missing/pending/loading chunks, and a producer followed by a cold GPU-cache consumer. The consumer only hits keys actually stored by the producer.

## Test Result

- Related suites: **474 passed** locally. Native H20: **378 passed**, then the remaining **96 passed** with `--lf` after seeding the missing public `facebook/opt-125m` config/tokenizer cache and enabling offline mode; no code changes.
- Focused regressions: **102 passed**. With only the production file reverted to base `de500290ffffeb7bd834872c0dea5331590dd40d`: **14 failed, 88 passed**.
- Pre-commit, including mypy 3.10, and the explicit mypy 3.12 hook: passed.

```python
"""Tiny Step3.5 two-module MTP, real GPU kernels and CPU offload transfers."""
import os
os.environ['VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING']='0'
os.environ['VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER']='1'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.step3p5 import Step3p5Config

model_dir=Path('/tmp/vllm-offload-mtp-smoke')
Step3p5Config(hidden_size=128, intermediate_size=256, num_attention_heads=2,
    num_attention_groups=1, head_dim=64, num_hidden_layers=2, vocab_size=256,
    max_position_embeddings=256, max_seq_len=256, sliding_window=32,
    num_nextn_predict_layers=2, moe_layers_enum='1', moe_num_experts=2,
    moe_top_k=1, moe_intermediate_size=128, share_expert_dim=128,
    architectures=['Step3p5ForCausalLM']).save_pretrained(model_dir)
llm=LLM(model=str(model_dir),skip_tokenizer_init=True,load_format='dummy',
    enforce_eager=True,dtype='bfloat16',seed=42,max_model_len=256,
    max_num_seqs=2,max_num_batched_tokens=256,gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
    kv_cache_memory_bytes=16<<20, block_size=16,enable_prefix_caching=True,
    disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False,compilation_config={'mode':0},
    kernel_config={'enable_jit_warmup':False},
    speculative_config={'method':'mtp','num_speculative_tokens':4},
    kv_transfer_config={'kv_connector':'OffloadingConnector','kv_role':'kv_both',
        'kv_connector_extra_config':{'cpu_bytes_to_use':16<<20}})
try:
    core=llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core
    cfg=core.vllm_config
    assert cfg.speculative_config.use_multi_module_mtp()
    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.multi_module_mtp.speculator import MultiModuleMTPSpeculator
    runner=core.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
    speculator=runner.speculator
    assert isinstance(speculator,MultiModuleMTPSpeculator),type(speculator)
    proposal_trace=[]
    force_rejections=os.environ.get('FORCE_DRAFT_REJECTIONS')=='1'
    original_propose=speculator.propose
    def track_propose(*args,**kwargs):
        batch=kwargs.get('input_batch',args[0] if args else None)
        rejected=kwargs.get('num_rejected',args[6] if len(args)>6 else None)
        proposal_trace.append({'has_prefill':bool(batch.has_prefill),
            'num_rejected':rejected[:batch.num_reqs].tolist()})
        drafts=original_propose(*args,**kwargs)
        if force_rejections:
            drafts.fill_(75)
        return drafts
    speculator.propose=track_propose
    connector=core.scheduler.connector.connector_scheduler
    specs=[g.kv_cache_spec for g in connector.config.kv_group_configs]
    assert any(isinstance(s,SlidingWindowSpec) and s.extra_retained_tokens==3 for s in specs)
    load_keys=[]
    original_load=connector.manager.prepare_load
    def track_load(keys,ctx):
        keys=list(keys)
        load_keys.append(len(keys))
        return original_load(keys,ctx)
    connector.manager.prepare_load=track_load
    prompt={'prompt_token_ids':list(range(10,75))}
    params=SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=16,ignore_eos=True)
    cold=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    for _ in range(1000):
        if not core.scheduler.has_requests(): break
        core.step()
    assert not core.scheduler.has_requests()
    assert llm.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)
    warm=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    assert cold.outputs[0].token_ids==warm.outputs[0].token_ids
    assert warm.num_cached_tokens>0 and load_keys
    assert any(not call['has_prefill'] for call in proposal_trace)
    if force_rejections:
        assert any(max(call['num_rejected'])>1 for call in proposal_trace)
    result={'proposal_trace':proposal_trace,'force_draft_rejections':force_rejections,
        'speculator_class':type(speculator).__name__,'cold':cold.outputs[0].token_ids,'warm':warm.outputs[0].token_ids,
        'cached_tokens':warm.num_cached_tokens,'load_chunk_counts':load_keys,
        'kv_specs':[str(s) for s in specs],'weights':'dummy',
        'mtp_modules':2,'speculative_tokens':4,'model_runner':'V2'}
    Path('../tiny_mtp_v2_rejection_result.json' if force_rejections else '../tiny_mtp_v2_result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(result))
finally:
    llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown()
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make GPU sync checks safe under torch.compile
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`gpu_sync_debug`'s patched tensor-copy wrappers currently read a `ContextVar`
before checking whether Dynamo is tracing. A full-graph compile therefore fails
with an unsupported `ContextVar.get()` instead of bypassing sync checks as
intended.

This change:

- checks `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` before accessing either `ContextVar`;
- routes the original C++ `Tensor.to` descriptor through a weak-referenceable
  Python callable registered with `torch.compiler.allow_in_graph`, so Dynamo
  treats the call as opaque while AOT/Inductor can still lower it;
- adds a full-graph `torch.compile` regression with device and dtype derived
  dynamically from another tensor;
- runs the two new Voxtral CUDA-graph parameter cases in explicitly spawned
  processes so neither prior pytest CUDA state nor the other graph mode can
  contaminate them.

## CI incident and test-selection evidence

Daily main build #88920 first exposed this in
`test_voxtral_realtime_cudagraph[FULL_DECODE_ONLY]` in the H200 Multimodal
Models (Extended Generation 1) job. PR #51167 added the compiled Voxtral path,
but that exact job was blocked in both its PR build #88857 and post-merge main
build #88899, so the failure was not exercised before the daily run.

I searched open vLLM issues and PRs for the exact `ContextVar.get` / Voxtral
full-graph failure and did not find an existing fix.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/gpu_sync_debug.py tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py` — passed all applicable hooks
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Local pytest was not run because this regression requires CUDA and this development host has no GPU.
- Exact H200 build #88941 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker but exposed the
  saved C++ `Tensor.to` descriptor as Dynamo-unsupported in the Voxtral
  full-graph test.
- Replacement #88962 proved that registering the method descriptor directly
  is invalid at import time because `allow_in_graph` stores a weak reference.
- Replacement #88969 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker and the original Voxtral
  `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` compile/CUDA-graph surface at literal head `c2fbacb1`.
  The following `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` parameter then hit the normal startup
  guard with only 25.73/32.5 GiB free after the prior in-process compiled
  runner retained about 6.5 GiB; later failures were cascades from that state.
- Replacement #89000 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker, but the default CUDA
  isolation helper chose `fork` after the parent pytest process had initialized
  CUDA. Both Voxtral cases therefore failed before engine compilation with
  `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`.
- #89010 used an invalid copied full SHA and failed in bootstrap; it contains
  no test evidence.
- #89011 also passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker, then reproduced the same two
  pre-compilation CUDA-fork failures. Its literal head still contained the
  helper's default mode because the intended one-line `spawn` edit had not
  been staged into the prior commit.
- Current exact replacement #89026 runs only the same two H200 lanes at
  literal signed head `f7f21d97caecf810db069402ed02c4624311af32`, which
  explicitly passes `method="spawn"` to the isolation helper.

No model evaluation is required because the production change only alters
debug-wrapper control flow while Dynamo is tracing. The exact affected
generation test is included in targeted CI.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was prepared with AI assistance. Human review is required before
this draft is marked ready or merged.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Honor device_ids for worker device placement
commits.pr_body:
### Issue
`XPUWorker.init_device` directly binds `torch.device(f"xpu:{local_rank}")`, ignoring the engine's resolved `device_ids` (`parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`).

As a result, `--device-ids` (or `LLM(device_ids=...)`) had no effect on XPU: every single‑GPU worker landed on visible ordinal `0`, regardless of the requested device.

### Fix
This mirrors the CUDA worker changes from #45026:

- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`: remove the XPU-specific no-op branch in `_set_visible_devices` so DP engine-core actors set `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` on XPU too, matching the CUDA path.
- `vllm/v1/worker/xpu_worker.py`: rework the `local_rank` bound-check asserts to account for `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` when present, falling back to the raw visible device count otherwise.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Tolerate NaN-corrupted logprobs in engine-core
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a total-outage bug in the Rust frontend's engine-core client: a single request asking for `logprobs`/`prompt_logprobs` while the model produces NaN logits permanently kills the client — `/health` returns 503 and every subsequent request (including ones with no logprobs) fails with `engine-core error: messagepack ext value decode failed: token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs` until process restart.

Rank 0 is an engine output that must be accepted: the sampler computes the rank as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), which is 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN because every `>=` comparison against NaN is false. The decode failure is frame-scoped (one bad row fails the whole batched `EngineCoreOutputs` payload), happens on the shared output-reader path, and is recorded as a sticky health error, so a per-request data anomaly becomes a server-wide outage.

**Fix:** in `PositionLogprobs::from_decoded_row`, accept and preserve `sampled_rank = 0` along with the engine's original logprob values. This keeps decoding valid for the other requests in the batch. The existing Rust OpenAI serving helper converts NaN and negative infinity to `-9999.0` when constructing HTTP responses; engine-core decoding preserves the numerical results for all consumers.

**Why this does not duplicate existing PRs:**
- #48585 fixes the same *class* of defect (non-finite logprobs reaching the serving layer) but in the **Python** frontend, and for logprob *values*, not ranks. This PR addresses the Rust engine-client rank-zero decode failure; the Rust HTTP helper already handles NaN and negative infinity.
- #50725 is a different code path (process abort from an empty stop string); it only shares the blast-radius pattern.
- #50002 proposed aborting requests on optional NaN detection and was superseded by #50283; this PR handles rank-zero payloads that reach the frontend.
- #45060 establishes all-NaN logits as a real engine state vLLM already handles elsewhere.

Healthy payloads retain their existing behavior. Model evaluation N/A: this changes wire-payload decode tolerance while preserving the engine's numerical output.

AI assistance was used for the original fix and the follow-up changes and tests. The follow-up preserves rank 0 and raw engine values and adds coverage for the existing HTTP conversion.

## Test Plan

Two regression tests cover the layer boundary:

1. `zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates` decodes a shared `EngineCoreOutputs` batch, preserving rank 0, NaN, and negative infinity in both sample and prompt logprobs while keeping the healthy request intact.
2. `chat_logprobs_clamps_nan_and_negative_infinity_for_json` verifies that the existing OpenAI response conversion emits `-9999.0` for NaN and negative infinity while preserving a finite logprob.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server -E 'package(vllm-engine-core-client) | test(routes::openai::utils::logprobs::tests)'`: **118 passed**.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and commit-time pre-commit hooks: passed.

Commands ran from `rust/` with a fresh short `TMPDIR` for tests and an existing Cargo target directory. No GPU was required.

Model evaluation N/A: the change preserves the engine's numerical output and adjusts frontend decode tolerance.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Enable a4w4 flydsl kernels for KimiK3

## Summary

- When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1` (the existing Kimi-K3 recipe toggle), route SiTU MXFP4 routed experts through AITER's **a4w4** flydsl kernels (`afp4_wfp4_fp4`, `fp4q`) instead of the previous **a8w4** path (`afp8_wfp4_fp8`, `fp8q`, `_gui_` interleave).
- vLLM sets `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=1` at init and clears any legacy `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` override (AITER checks A8W4 first, so leaving it set would still pick afp8).
- SiTUv2 gate/up weights use the **separated** layout to match ATOM kernel selection.

No new env flags; the existing recipe variable keeps its name for compatibility.

## AITER requirement

This path needs [ROCm/aiter#4463](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4463) (first tagged in **AITER v0.1.20**): `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` dispatch plus `kimik3_a4w4_{un,}tuned_fmoe.csv`. vLLM `main` already pins `AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.21.post1`, which includes that PR.

On AITER **v0.1.19** (this PR's original docker pin), a4w4 still launches `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` but logs **heuristic FlyDSL fallback** because the tuned CSV rows are missing. That is not the tuned a4w4 config from #4463.

## Motivation

Trace comparison on Kimi-K3 / MI355X shows vLLM dispatching `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp8_wfp4_fp8_*_gui_xcd4_*` while ATOM uses `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp4_wfp4_fp4_*_situv2_*`. AITER supports a4w4 via `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` in #4463; vLLM previously wired the recipe toggle to a8w4. Open PR #50813 adds explicit opt-in a8w4 for Quark checkpoints — this change makes a4w4 the default for the existing SiTUv2 recipe path.

## Results

GSM8K (Kimi-K3 MXFP4, MI355X, TP=8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`, greedy 5-shot, full test split `n=1319`):

| Filter | Metric | This PR (a4w4) | Prior a8w4 recipe |
|---|---|---|---|
| strict-match | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |
| flexible-extract | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |

No accuracy regression (within stderr). Decode dispatch used `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` (fp4 activations); no `afp8` / `_gui_` kernels.

`niah_single_2` at 32k (`n=20`): **1.0** on both a4w4 and a8w4.

8k ISL / 1k OSL serving on AITER **without** #4463 tuned CSVs (heuristic a4w4 vs tuned a8w4) is a wash (~0.5% at conc 4/8). Isolated kernel timings in AITER #4463 show a4w4 ahead of a8w4 once the tuned rows are present.

## Test plan

- [x] Serve Kimi-K3 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`; confirm a4w4 FlyDSL (`afp4_wfp4_bf16`, not `afp8` / `fp8q` / `_gui_`)

- [x] `niah_single_2` vs prior a8w4

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] [Bugfix] Enable Load and Inference of GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 Checkpoint
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Quark checkpoint `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, global MXFP4 quant with attention projections kept as source block-FP8/BF16). Two independent bugs break weight load. This PR fixes both and the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint now loads and serves with accuracy on par with the source checkpoint (`zai/GLM-5.3-Flash`).

## Bugs

1. Dense-MLP `gate_up_proj` resolves to the wrong quant scheme:
The class inherits `packed_modules_mapping = {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]}` from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration`. This identity mapping is correct for GLM-4.1V (whose checkpoint stores a pre-fused `gate_up_proj` tensor), but GLM-5.3-Flash stores gate/up as **separate** tensors (both the [Quark ](https://huggingface.co/amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4)and the [base](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) checkpoints). With the identity entry, `QuarkConfig` falls back to `global_quant_config` (MXFP4) instead of the per-layer block-FP8 in `layer_quant_config` and builds the layer as MXFP4 and mismatches the FP8 checkpoint tensor at load.


2. MLA projection scale name mismatch:
The MLA `q_a` / `kv_a` / `q_b` / `o` projections are dequantized on load by `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, which only recognized scales named `weight_scale_inv`. Quark checkpoints export `weight_scale`, so the scale fell through and the fused-qkv-a stacked mapping could not find its target.

## Changes (`vllm/model_executor/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`)

1. Override `packed_modules_mapping` on `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` so the  fused `gate_up_proj` expands to its real shard names `["gate_proj", "up_proj"]` (matching the `Glm4vMoeForConditionalGeneration` sibling / `glm4_moe` / `deepseek_v2`).
2. In `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, accept the Quark scale name:
   `is_scale = "weight_scale_inv" in name or name.endswith(".weight_scale")`.

## Related PRs and Issues:

Bug 1 was initially reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54641, and PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54702 was opened with a fix attempt, which ***does not*** necessarily address the root cause. It makes Quark tolerate identity mappings by looking up the *fused* name in `layer_quant_config`, but this checkpoint keys the *split* names, so it still falls back to MXFP4 and crashes.

An open PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54556 proposes a fix for an issue similar to Bug 2 for GLM-5.3, but via a remap in `deepseek_v2.py` for the *full* GLM-5.3 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) model, which doesn't reach ***GLM-5.3-Flash*** path (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). 

Another previously merged PR (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54770) wires `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` to register `weight_scale`, so *quantized* modules can load natively. However, it can't cover bug 2 here since GLM-5.3-Flash keeps the MLA projections **BF16** and dequantizes the FP8 checkpoint tensors manually.

## Test Results
Changes tested on 4x AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs

```bash
# Serve:
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enforce-eager \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --port <port> --trust-remote-code

# Eval:
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/completions,tokenizer=amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048
```

| Checkpoint | before | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` | fails to load (AssertionError, then KeyError) | **gsm8k strict exact_match 0.9219** |
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`  | loads |  **gsm8k strict exact_match 0.9121** |

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix decode instance's multi-layer MTP kv caches during P/D
commits.pr_body: ## Context During multi-module MTP with P/D, the prefill instance runs prefill on the full prompt and the last N MTP layers each generate a draft token. This is problematic on the last prefill chunk, because MTP layer i will embed its draft token into MTP layer i + 1. Those draft tokens are unverified, and remain in the KV cache for those last N-1 MTP layers. See the visualization below: During standalone serving, the next decode step would receive the number of rejections, and would re-prefill those stale cache slots accordingly. During P/D, the decode instance doesn't receive this information, and thus the unverified draft tokens remain in the KV cache, hurting acceptance rates. ## This PR Generalizes the 1-token backoff used by Mamba to skip prefilling the last token on the prefill instance, and recompute that token on the decode instance, for multi-module MTP. Now, the prefill instance no longer pollutes the last N-1 MTP modules with unverified draft tokens, and the decode instance completes prefill for the last N-1 prompt tokens. I created a helper method in `VllmConfig` called `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` that is used to get the number of MTP modules, and use them for this prefill backoff. It is now called by several other callsites to reduce code duplication. ## Benchmarks Inkling-Small-NVFP4, 1P1D on one 4×GB200 node (prefill GPUs 0,1 / decode GPUs 2,3, TP=2 each), `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}`, SPEED-Bench `throughput_16k`/`low_entropy`, 2048 in / 2048 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts. Acceptance read from the decode instance's `/metrics`. | Metric | Before (`ae71862c51`) | After (`5ee6a77da2`) | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | **acceptance_length** | **1.0891** | **3.5207** | **+2.4316** | | **acceptance_rate** | **1.11%** | **31.51%** | **+30.40** | | Total token throughput | 3,520 tok/s | 12,156 tok/s | +245% | | Mean TPOT | 35.67 ms | 9.99 ms | −72% | | Mean E2EL | 73.6 s | 20.5 s | −72% | | Benchmark wall time | 634.8 s | 204.4 s | −68% | | Position | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Before | .0259 | .0179 | .0132 | .0095 | .0074 | .0060 | .0050 | .0042 | | After | .6745 | .4802 | .3575 | .2806 | .2282 | .1917 | .1644 | .1436 | Both arms completed 512/512 requests with 0 failures on identical input (1,048,576 tokens). Output token counts differ by 2.3%. An acceptance length of 1.089 means ~99% of drafts were rejected. Speculative decoding was effectively inert under P/D before the fix.

commits.pr_title: [Build][NVIDIA] Update public Rubin dependencies and MSA compatibility
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Update public Rubin dependencies and the MSA revision for Quack/CuTe DSL compatibility.

- Pin CUDA Python/bindings to 13.4.1, Quack to 0.6.5, FlashInfer Python/cubin to 0.6.18.post1, its CUDA 13.4 JIT cache to 0.6.18.post1+cu134, and NIXL to 1.4.1. Add the official FlashInfer indexes.
- Advance the official MSA revision to `f355c37eb4e1413f21ee2ad8bbad25079e6bef9d`, incorporating [MSA#12](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA/pull/12).
- Handle Quack alongside the existing Rubin exclusions from standard CUDA wheel metadata, keeping its Rubin pin in `rubin-prerelease.txt`. This is the only Dockerfile change; standard CUDA requirements also now pin Quack 0.6.5 after the upstream merge.
- Advance to the newest compatible CUDA 13.4 Torch/Torchvision/Torchaudio nightlies available when checked on September 12, 2026 UTC:

| Package | aarch64 | x86_64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| torch | `2.15.0.dev20260908+cu134` | `2.15.0.dev20260909+cu134` |
| torchvision | `0.30.0.dev20260909+cu134` | `0.30.0.dev20260909+cu134` |
| torchaudio | `2.11.0.dev20260911+cu134` | `2.11.0.dev20260911+cu134` |

Torch September 11 is available, but no published CUDA 13.4 Torchvision wheel pairs with it. The latest Torchvision wheels require Torch September 8 on aarch64 and September 9 on x86_64. Torchaudio September 11 uses `cp310-abi3` wheels compatible with Python 3.12 and requires `torch>=2.11`.

Keep CUTLASS DSL `4.8.0.dev0` and remove the requirements-file `--pre` option that uv ignores. The selected Torch wheels still require Triton `3.8.0+gitc01b6774`.

### Related work

Duplicate searches covered open Rubin dependency PRs and #49735. #55953 includes Torch wheel-pairing work as part of Rubin nightly publishing; this PR adds no release pipeline changes. #54927 merged the standard CUDA dependency updates, #54355 concerns optional KV connectors, and #56489 is a broader dependency update. This PR combines the Rubin-specific dependency set with the MSA compatibility revision.

## Validation

The aarch64 CUDA 13.4 image built successfully from current PR commit `89c93256fafe9541aadafa63b7a202d9fdc0f7df`. Both model tests use this same image; no production source patches or package metadata overrides were applied during validation.

- `git diff --check` and targeted pre-commit passed.
- Public wheel metadata and bounded Python 3.12 resolver controls passed for both aarch64 and x86_64. GPU runtime validation covers aarch64 only.
- Installed pins and exact MSA source were verified. CPU/CUDA Torchvision NMS, Torchaudio import and CPU resampling, all-four-GPU numerical Triton kernels, fresh `torch.compile`, and shared-library linkage checks passed.
- Direct MSA numerical tests on one GPU passed sparse indexer/top-k selection, sparse decode including graph replay, and sparse prefill against independent references.

| Model | Configuration | Exact final-answer checks | Fixed GSM8K smoke |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` | TP4 | 20/20 | 15/16, invalid 0 |
| `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` | TP4, FP8 KV, CUTLASS MSA decode | 20/20 | 15/16, invalid 0 |

Frozen model revisions are `95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989` for Qwen and `901464083161bf8612a29ff7ad29914cd4ab4a85` for MiniMax. Exact-answer checks cover short requests, long-context retrieval and 16 batched arithmetic completions. GSM8K uses the first 16 questions, five-shot chat, temperature 0, seed 42 and a 1024-token output limit. These are smoke tests, not full accuracy or performance benchmarks.

Qwen returned complete, readable responses. Its missed GSM8K question confused the break-even year with the first profitable year; three batched explanations contain arithmetic inconsistencies despite correct final answers. MiniMax also returned complete, readable responses and missed the same GSM8K question. One batch explanation mislabels a digit position, and another GSM8K explanation confuses cleaners remaining with cleaners sold despite a correct final answer. Independent raw CUDA trace review confirmed MSA indexer/top-k, CuTe sparse prefill and native CUTLASS sparse decode on all four workers during the controlled requests, including nontrivial long-context selection and actual batch-16 generation.

Additional checks retain failures:

- `uv pip check` rejects the public cuSPARSELt 0.8.1 wheel's internal `manylinux2014_sbsa` tag on aarch64. Its library is AArch64 ELF; this is not a claim of a dedicated cuSPARSELt numerical test.
- Optional `nixl_ep` import fails because NIXL 1.4.1 lacks its Torch 2.15 extension. Ordinary NIXL import passes. TP4 serving does not establish EP support.

The original runtime aggregate and both serving aggregates retain exit 1. Each serving scanner matched caught optional NIXL-EP warning tracebacks; all functional request/evaluation subprocesses and final server health checks passed. MiniMax also logged repeated multicast/`CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED` workspace warnings and a FlashInfer all-reduce norm fusion initialization error. Serving continued, but this test does not establish availability of that collective optimization.

### Build and serve

Commands use generic local paths and names. Both base and final targets were built sequentially to avoid concurrent cold-cache wheel installation contention.

```bash
docker buildx create --name rubin-validation --driver docker-container \
  --driver-opt network=host,image=moby/buildkit:v0.20.0
build_args=(
  --builder rubin-validation --progress=plain
  --file docker/Dockerfile --platform linux/arm64
  --build-arg BUILD_BASE_IMAGE=pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda13.4
  --build-arg FINAL_BASE_IMAGE=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.08-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04
  --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=13.4 --build-arg INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE=true
  --build-arg TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REPO=https://github.com/triton-lang/triton.git
  --build-arg TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REVISION=c01b6774b1865984607d89d89d3a10833de92037
  --build-arg torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0
  --build-arg max_jobs=32 --build-arg nvcc_threads=2
  --build-arg RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false
)
docker buildx build "${build_args[@]}" --target base .
docker buildx build "${build_args[@]}" --target vllm-openai --load -t vllm-rubin:pr .
```

Both models run sequentially with separate model/kernel caches. The variables below are generic absolute local paths, populated with the pinned model snapshots before launch. Stop the Qwen container after its tests before launching MiniMax on the same GPUs.

```bash
run_model() {
  docker run --detach --name "$NAME" --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host \
    --env NVIDIA_DISABLE_REQUIRE=1 --env VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=1 \
    --env VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
    --volume "$MODEL_CACHE:/work/huggingface:ro" \
    --env HF_HOME=/work/huggingface --env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
```

## Purpose

Enable attention HMA with pipeline-parallel prefill in `NixlPushConnector`,
following #45880. Producer PP stages and a PP1 decoder may pool the same layers
into different physical KV-cache regions. This PR matches layers by name and
builds descriptors using each side's region geometry.

This updates the existing push-mode PR. Pull-mode work in #43368/#48263 and
the earlier #47981 prototype use different implementations. Packed MLA is the
stacked follow-up #50499, which should land after this PR.

## Design and rebase

- `NixlAgentMetadata.region_members` advertises layer names; wire version **11 → 12**.
- Registration derives `_transfer_layer_names`, `_transfer_layer_region_indices`,
  and `_transfer_layer_group_ids` per worker. `_supports_pp_hma` expresses the
  connector capability; `_requires_layer_name_routing()` applies runtime gates.
- Remote layer alignment selects this PP stage's layers and reorders addresses,
  lengths, strides, capacities, group IDs, names, and memory types. Missing or
  duplicate layers and inconsistent metadata fail explicitly.
- Descriptors use cumulative per-region capacities; physical allocations are
  registered once. PP1 and non-HMA layouts retain region-index routing.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Add sampled filtering for persistent top-k
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Speed up long FP32 sparse-indexer decode top-k with sampling inspired by [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect). A coalesced sample estimates a cutoff, survivors are compacted in shared memory, and exact FP32 selection finishes on those candidates. Too few or too many candidates trigger exact full-row selection.

Enable sampling above 64 rows, with **actual valid length ≥98,304 for k=512 or ≥65,536 for k=1024/2048**, and at least 144 KiB opt-in shared memory. Shorter runtime rows reuse the existing selector within the same launch. These conservative bounds come from the fine B300 sweep below.

![B300 measured crossover envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/9b766447102d21b87cfee5856be43d9a036a9eb4/crossover_envelope.png)

The plot forces sampling to expose the crossover; it shows the minimum speedup across measured batches, allocations, seeds and cache modes. The k=512 slowdown near 80K–86K motivates its later cutoff.

Final dispatch improves every tested case entirely within the sampling region. At B=1024 with 80–100% ragged lengths, warm latency drops **316.58→207.06 µs** at 128K/k=2048 and **584.45→301.72 µs** at 256K/k=512. Short-row fallback can add up to **3.32%**; the largest absolute increase measured was **1.215 µs**. Performance validation is B300-only.

Duplicate checks found no open PR implementing this sampled filter: #44606 tunes existing dispatch, #55872 adds a FlashInfer backend, and #55314 fixes existing stash overflow. That overflow remains outside the new path. Prefill is unchanged.

## Test Plan

Added graph-replay correctness coverage and `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_persistent_topk.py` for full/ragged lengths and warm/cold L2. All GPU runs used `chg` reservations and source-built baseline/candidate libraries.

commits.pr_title: [DSA] Wire DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits into the DeepSeek V4.1 indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4.1 selects attention tokens in two levels: one indexer layer publishes the top candidate blocks of the context, and the indexer layers after it pick their top-k inside those blocks. Today the consumer layers still score the **whole** context with dense MQA logits and then mask everything outside the candidates. DeepGEMM 2.8 ships sparse MQA-logits kernels (deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#432) that score only a given list of blocks, so this PR lets the consumer layers score just the candidate blocks. Their logits work goes from O(context) to O(candidate blocks), a fixed 16K positions for V4.1-Flash, and their top-k runs in that compressed space and is mapped back to context positions.

Design:

- **A separate indexer, not a branch in the dense one.** The consumer layers use a new `SparseMQAIndexer` layer with its own backend and attention metadata (`DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`, `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerMetadata`). It is a plain module rather than a custom op: V4.1 does not go through `torch.compile`, and the attention layer already runs the indexer inside its breakable-CUDA-graph eager segment. The dense `SparseAttnIndexer` op is untouched. The candidate-source layer and the indexers before it stay dense.
- **Every requirement is checked once, at engine start.** The metadata builder validates the model, the MXFP4 indexer cache, the GPU generation, the DeepGEMM version, the DeepSelect extension and the logits/top-k layout it needs, and raises a clear error instead of silently falling back per step. There is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path: the candidate expansion and the index remap are Triton kernels, the top-k is DeepSelect.
- **Nothing is allocated or recomputed on the hot path.** The builder owns the per-row scratch; the candidate-block expansion and the DeepGEMM schedule depend only on the candidates, which are identical for all consumer layers of a step, so the first consumer computes them and the others reuse them through the shared metadata.
- **No dtype casts on the hot path.** The sparse kernels take bf16 weights and emit bf16 logits. The fused Q RoPE-quant kernel that produces the per-head weights writes them in bf16 for this indexer (fp32 for the dense one), and DeepSelect (#56464) runs the top-k on the bf16 logits directly.
- **Opt-in** via `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4", "indexer_sparse_logits": true}'`. Below ~16K tokens the candidates cover the whole context and the dense path is cheaper, so the default stays off; the feature is for long-context serving.
- **One KV-layout requirement.** DeepGEMM's paged kernels address pages as `base + page * stride` and need that stride 512B-aligned. In V4.1's block-major layout the stride is the whole block (all layers' pages), which is not 512-aligned. `MLAAttentionSpec` gains `block_stride_alignment`, and the block size is rounded up to it in the same place HiSparse already rounds it (`_get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block`). With the flag on this costs 0.8% of KV memory; with it off nothing changes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: candidate-expansion math and a randomized comparison of the Triton expansion against a PyTorch reference (including strided inputs); exact selected-value parity of the sparse path with `torch.topk` over dense bf16 logits masked to the candidates, for prefill and paged decode, including spec-decode rows, CUDA-graph capture/replay and schedule reuse by a later layer; kernel numerics vs a PyTorch fp32 reference. `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py`: the bf16 weights output of the fused Q kernel (Triton and CuTeDSL) equals the fp32 result rounded once. mypy and ruff via pre-commit.
- Kernel microbenchmark of the per-layer indexer pipeline (dense logits + mask + top-k vs sparse logits + top-k + remap) with an exact selected-value parity check, GB300, CUDA-graph replay.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4 on 4x GB300, MXFP4 indexer cache, greedy, prefix caching off, flag on vs off: decode and prefill throughput from 8K to 1M context, and long-context NLL.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 28 passed. The sparse kernels produce bitwise the same bf16 logits as the dense kernels on the candidate columns, so the tests assert that the sparse path selects exactly the same values per row as `torch.topk` over dense bf16 logits masked to the candidates; only tie order among equal values may differ.

**Kernel level** (GB300, speedup of the sparse indexer pipeline over the dense one per consumer layer; decode rows are one query per request, the prefill column is a chunk of query rows sharing their sequence's K. V4.1-Flash has 4 consumer layers, the first one also pays the once-per-step candidate expansion, which lowers its speedup by 20-50%):

| context | decode, batch 64 | decode, batch 256 | prefill chunk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K | 1.2x | 1.2x | 1.6x |
| 32K | 1.7x | 1.8x | 2.3x |
| 128K | 4.4x | 5.8x | 8.3x |
| 512K | 14.4x | 22.9x | |

**End to end** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4, 4x GB300; decode and prefill throughput of the whole batch, from a linear fit of wall time against output length):

| batch x context | decode tok/s off | decode tok/s on | decode speedup | prefill tok/s off | prefill tok/s on | prefill speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 x 8K | 5,570 | 5,895 | 1.06x | 68,712 | 65,541 | 0.95x |
| 32 x 100K | 3,263 | 3,434 | 1.05x | 60,508 | 64,306 | 1.06x |
| 16 x 256K | 2,055 | 2,153 | 1.05x | 48,504 | 57,670 | 1.19x |
| 8 x 512K | 1,057 | 1,107 | 1.05x | 34,127 | 48,805 | 1.43x |
| 4 x 1M | 568 | 583 | 1.03x | 16,261 | 32,517 | 2.00x |

Decode gets 3-6% faster: the indexer is only a few percent of a decode step at these batch sizes. Prefill is where the O(context) cost shows: the dense indexer's fp32 logits grow with the context and are chunked, written and read back several times, while the sparse rows stay 16K wide, so prefill throughput is 1.2x at 256K, 1.4x at 512K and 2x at 1M, while at 8K it is 5% slower.

**Accuracy** (78K-token real document, mean NLL of the next token by position; the sparse kernels score in bf16, the dense path in fp32). Two runs of the same configuration differ by up to 0.002 per bucket (TP=4 run-to-run noise), and on/off differ by the same amount:

| position | 0-16K | 16K-32K | 32K-64K | 64K-78K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| off | 0.4001 | 0.3715 | 0.3523 | 0.3735 |
| on | 0.4022 | 0.3706 | 0.3526 | 0.3755 |
| on, second run | 0.4010 | 0.3719 | 0.3534 | 0.3737 |

## Requirements and limitations

- SM100-class GPUs, DeepGEMM >= 2.8 (the repo pin is older; the flag fails at startup with a clear message on older builds), the DeepSelect extension (`vllm._deepselect_C`, built with vllm) and the MXFP4 indexer cache (the kernels take UE8M0 scales). `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend` must be `auto` or `deep_select`. Not supported with DCP/PCP.
- The sparse kernels score in bf16 with bf16 weights (no fp32 option), so the flag changes the indexer's score precision; greedy outputs are not token-identical to the dense path (see the NLL table).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Format kernel-import errors eagerly so warning_once does not retain them
commits.pr_body:
FIX #54096

## Purpose

`logger.warning_once` caches its arguments forever (`lru_cache`). The kernel import fallbacks passed the live `ImportError` as a lazy format argument, so the cache retained the exception — and through `__traceback__` every frame and local on the raising path. `import_kernels` runs inside `LLM.__init__`, so on platforms without compiled `vllm._C` kernels the pinned locals included the `LLM` instance under construction: it could never be garbage collected, its EngineCore subprocess only exited with the interpreter, and on accelerator plugins the device stayed held by the leaked engine. Each exception instance was also a distinct cache key, defeating the once-deduplication.

Per review feedback, this fixes the specific call sites and nothing else: format the exception eagerly at the five kernel import sites (`repr(e)` with `%s` renders byte-identical output to the previous `%r` of the live exception). No logger changes, no new tests.

## Test Plan

Block the `vllm._C` import with a meta-path finder, keep a weakref to the raised exception, call `Platform.import_kernels()` twice, then `gc.collect()`:

```python
import gc, sys, weakref
from vllm.platforms.interface import Platform

class TrackedError(ModuleNotFoundError):  # plain ModuleNotFoundError is not weakref-able
    pass

refs = []
class Blocker:
    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
        if name in ("vllm._C", "vllm._moe_C_stable_libtorch"):
            e = TrackedError(f"No module named '{name}'")
            refs.append(weakref.ref(e))
            raise e
        return None

for m in ("vllm._C", "vllm._moe_C_stable_libtorch"):
    sys.modules.pop(m, None)
sys.meta_path.insert(0, Blocker())

Platform.import_kernels()
Platform.import_kernels()  # second call: shows dedup behavior
gc.collect()
print("exception retained after gc:", any(r() is not None for r in refs))
```

## Test Result

Output before this fix (main):

```text
WARNING 09-14 21:12:50 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
WARNING 09-14 21:12:50 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
exception retained after gc: True
```

The warning fires on every call ("once" is defeated because each exception instance is a new cache key), and the exception is retained forever with its traceback.

Output after this fix:

```text
WARNING 09-14 21:10:57 [interface.py:368] Failed to import from vllm._C: TrackedError("No module named 'vllm._C'")
exception retained after gc: False
```

The warning text is byte-identical, fires once, and nothing is retained.

End-to-end: on a Neuron (OOT platform) stack with this fix applied, `del llm` shuts the EngineCore down within 2s; previously the engine survived until interpreter exit and held the device.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve per-layer offsets in KV cache bindings
commits.pr_body:
FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57019

## Purpose

Fix cross-layer KV overwrites when HiSparse packs multiple layers into one allocation. Both resident and hot bindings used the tensor's base offset for every layer, allowing later layers to overwrite earlier layers' cached rows. Compute `tensor.offset + layer_index * tensor.layer_stride` once per layer and use it in both bindings.

Addresses #57019; the faulty bindings were introduced by #53781.

Add a nightly HiSparse GSM8K job using the existing accuracy harness and real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` weights. It runs on four B200s with TP4, BF16 KV, eager execution, and a 32 GiB host pool. All 1,319 questions are evaluated with 5 shots and an explicit 90% minimum accuracy. The job is optional in regular CI, following the existing nightly-job convention. No new unit test or standalone evaluation harness is added.

Duplicate-work check: read #57019 and its comments, searched open PRs for `57019 in:body`, `HiSparse`, and `HiSparse offset`. No open PR addressing these missing layer offsets was found. The host-mirror replay work in #56158 addresses a separate failure path.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, validation, and this description. The human submitter is responsible for line-by-line review and independent test validation.

## Test Plan

Run the new nightly test:

```bash
chg run -g 4 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
```

```bash
chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -q
```

## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Avoid nested score cancellation handlers for /v1/score alias
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix nested cancellation and server-load accounting on the deprecated `/v1/score` alias. `create_score_v1()` applied `@with_cancellation` and `@load_aware_call`, then delegated to `create_score()`, which already applies both wrappers. A single request therefore created two disconnect listeners and incremented server load twice; one listener could consume the disconnect while the real score handler continued running, leaving the load counter nonzero. Removing the two outer alias decorators makes `/v1/score` rely on the canonical `/score` handler's wrappers.

## Relationship to PR #55602

[PR #55602](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55602) removed redundant cancellation wrappers from the `/v1/rerank` and `/v2/rerank` aliases. This PR applies the same narrow delegation principle to `/v1/score` and additionally removes its redundant load-accounting wrapper. It does not change shared helpers or canonical score/rerank handlers.

## Reproducer

Run the following on upstream `main` and on this branch:

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.scoring.api_router import create_score_v1


async def main():
    disconnects = asyncio.Queue()
    handler_started = asyncio.Event()
    handler_cancelled = asyncio.Event()
    receive_calls = 0

    async def receive():
        nonlocal receive_calls
        receive_calls += 1
        return await disconnects.get()

    async def handler(request, raw_request):
        handler_started.set()
        try:
            await asyncio.Future()
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            handler_cancelled.set()
            raise

    state = SimpleNamespace(
        enable_server_load_tracking=True,
        server_load_metrics=0,
        serving_scores=handler,
    )
    raw_request = SimpleNamespace(
        app=SimpleNamespace(state=state),
        receive=receive,
    )

    route_task = asyncio.create_task(create_score_v1(None, raw_request))
    await asyncio.wait_for(handler_started.wait(), 1)
    for _ in range(100):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

    print(
        "before_disconnect",
        f"receive_calls={receive_calls}",
        f"load={state.server_load_metrics}",
    )
    await disconnects.put({"type": "http.disconnect"})
    print("route_result", await asyncio.wait_for(route_task, 1))
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    print(
        "after_disconnect",
        f"handler_cancelled={handler_cancelled.is_set()}",
        f"load={state.server_load_metrics}",
    )

    current = asyncio.current_task()
    pending = [task for task in asyncio.all_tasks() if task is not current]
    for task in pending:
        task.cancel()
    await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)


asyncio.run(main())
PY
```

## Output on main

```text
before_disconnect receive_calls=2 load=2
route_result None
after_disconnect handler_cancelled=False load=1
```

## Output on branch

```text
before_disconnect receive_calls=1 load=1
route_result None
after_disconnect handler_cancelled=True load=0
```

```bash
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py \
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Stabilize sparse-MLA DCP for GLM PCP evals
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Make the B200 GLM-5.2 PCP evaluation complete reliably across its TP/PCP/DCP configurations.

Exact main build [#89033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89033#01a0a3bf-3adb-4bec-82f2-da92bed83c19) first exposed two independent memory-budget failures after merged backend repair #56677. Successive literal-head and actual-branch gates then exposed the workspace, empty-rank, warmup-key, packed-pointer, and backend-combination edges described below.

## Root causes and fixes

### TP2/PCP2 autotuning headroom

FlashInfer CUTLASS autotuning requests 12.22 GiB with only about 7.6 GiB free after the implicit 0.92 budget reserves 33.46 GiB for KV cache. Set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` to leave about 12.5 GiB more autotuning headroom.

### TP1/PCP4/DCP4 KV-cache budget

CUDA graph profiling accounts for 6.15 GiB and reports total non-KV memory of 161.16 GiB, leaving a negative 3.23 GiB KV budget at 0.92. The runtime calculates 0.9545 as the utilization needed to preserve the old effective KV budget. Set 0.96, which produces a positive KV-cache budget.

### FlashInfer sparse-MLA DCP workspace

Under DCP, the TRTLLM-gen launcher requests LSE and carves a softmax-stats slab proportional to gathered heads and scheduled tokens. The old fixed workspace was 413,138,944 bytes; an earlier gate requested 470,810,624 bytes during warmup and failed before evaluation.

This PR carries Jason Yao's byte-derived sizing fix from #50791 with its original author commit, then adapts it to current main's split sparse-MLA backends: preallocation occurs only in `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` (SM100), so the separate SM120 backend keeps its own behavior. Explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` overrides remain respected and warn if undersized; non-DCP allocation is unchanged.

The GLM DCP eval now caps `--max-num-batched-tokens` at its existing 4,096-token model length. With 64 heads per TP1 rank and DCP4, that bounds the computed workspace to exactly 2,561,671,168 bytes (2.39 GiB) rather than 16.39 GiB at the previous 32,768-token scheduler cap. This preserves the evaluation's context-length and accuracy contract while keeping the up-front buffer inside the measured B200 reserve.

### Zero-local-sequence DCP warmup rank

CUDA graph warmup can give one DCP rank no local sequences while its padded LSE buffer still has rows. The eager empty-shard mask previously clamped the derived sequence index to `-1` and indexed an empty `seq_lens` tensor. When the statically shaped sequence count is zero, the mask now fills every padded LSE row with `-inf` and returns before the generic lookup. A focused CPU regression covers the exact shape.

### PCP+DCP first-request JIT keys

Actual-branch gate [#89065](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89065) showed DCP4 clearing engine initialization and graph capture, then stalling its first real inference batch after an unexpected `BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel` JIT. PCP chunk plans normalize this dispatch to `(DCP_RANK=0, DCP_WORLD=1)`, while startup warmup previously compiled only the configured per-process `(rank, world=4)` key. Warmup now includes both key families.

Actual-branch gate [#89083](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89083) narrowed the remaining miss: the PCP plan stores `global_cu` as the second row of one packed `3 x (rows+1)` allocation, so that input pointer is not always 16-byte aligned. Warmup had modeled alignment only for `uncompressed_seq_lens` and always replayed `global_cu` as aligned. It now covers the Cartesian product of both runtime alignment classes for both pointers, alongside the normalized DCP key.

### Unsupported FlashInfer sparse-MLA PCP+DCP combination

Actual-branch [#89087](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89087) proved the preceding fixes: TP2/PCP2 and TP1/PCP4 passed; DCP4 initialized with 29.45 GiB of KV cache, completed graph capture with no late JIT, and then hung on its first real batch. Diagnostic [#89089](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89089) reproduced the stall with NCCL tracing. The first PCP+DCP request had 153 query rows on rank 0 and 160 on ranks 1-3; the final DCP all-gather consequently entered with counts 9,792 versus 10,240 (`query_rows x 64 heads`).

The selected `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` backend filters top-k KV indices to the local DCP shard and returns LSE for every rank-local PCP query, but does not gather the full cross-DCP KV context first. The shared sparse-MLA wrapper then attempts to DCP-combine unequal PCP query-row tensors. `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` is the implementation that gathers each DCP KV shard before running rank-local PCP prefill queries and returns only the decode LSE that needs DCP combination.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend.supports_combination` now rejects combined PCP+DCP. Automatic selection therefore falls back to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`; an explicit incompatible backend request receives an actionable error. CPU regressions cover both rejection of the combined mode and continued support for PCP-only and DCP-only modes.

### DCP decode rank scalar

Actual-branch gate [#89093](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89093) confirmed the backend fix: DCP selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, completed graph capture and warmup, and began serving mixed prefill/decode traffic. The first decode then hit the runtime sync guard because `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` constructed the static integer DCP rank as a new device tensor inside metadata `build()`.

The metadata builder now materializes that scalar once on its device during initialization and passes the tensor through the localization helper. The helper accepts and directly reuses a correctly typed, colocated scalar tensor; a CPU regression replaces `torch.tensor` with a hard failure during this path to prove that no per-build scalar construction remains.

## Existing work / duplicate check

- #50781 is the exact workspace issue. Open #50791 contains the original diagnosis and implementation, but its head predates the separate TRTLLM/SM120 metadata builders. Original authorship and DCO trailers are preserved here; the current-main adaptation is a separate signed-off commit.
- Searches found no open PR or issue for the empty-rank mask, normalized PCP+DCP warmup key, packed-pointer alignment miss, or unsupported FlashInfer combined-mode selection.
- #56677 is merged and the exact gates confirm its `ag_rs` backend repair is active.
- Open #55828 addresses device-wide versus per-process memory attribution under co-tenancy. These builds use one worker per B200 and report identical per-rank accounting, so it does not own these deterministic config budgets.

## Validation

- Negative control: main #89033 reached both configs; TP2/PCP2 failed in CUTLASS autotuning and TP1/PCP4/DCP4 failed with a negative KV-cache budget.
- Intermediate exact gate #89040 at `a4149f66f`: both PCP configurations passed their corrected budget stages, then reproduced #50781 at the fixed workspace boundary.
- Diagnostic literal-head #89050: TP2/PCP2 and TP1/PCP4 passed, DCP4 received a positive 29.45-GiB KV cache, and warmup isolated the zero-local-sequence failure. It is not counted as a PR-branch gate because it was attributed to `main`.
- Actual-branch #89065 at `2f9bdae78`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 cleared sizing, initialization, and graph warmup, then exposed the normalized JIT-key miss.
- #89076 at `2d93cf0ef` was infrastructure-only: its Buildkite pre-commit proxy received a GitHub API 504, so no B200 job ran.
- Actual-branch #89083 at `2d93cf0ef`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 reached its first real request and isolated the remaining rank-0 unaligned-pointer JIT key.
- Actual-branch #89087 at `5d2d5c905`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 completed sizing, initialization, graph capture, and all warmups with no late JIT, then isolated the incompatible backend collective.
- Diagnostic #89089 at `5d2d5c905`: NCCL tracing recorded the exact unequal DCP all-gather counts (9,792 vs 10,240) on the first PCP+DCP request.
- `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py`: 10 passed.
- Focused zero-local-sequence regression: passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py -k indexer_warmup`: 2 passed.
- Both YAML files parse; `server_args` contain exactly the intended memory-utilization and scheduler-cap values.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks (including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and forbidden-import checks) and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Actual-branch #89093 at `7b2f95468`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, completed startup, served mixed prefill/decode traffic, and then exposed the runtime DCP-rank scalar construction in decode localization.
- `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py -k get_dcp_local_seq_lens`: 13 passed.
- Final actual-branch exact [#89097](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89097) passed terminally at `05d607a8b`: bootstrap, GitHub pre-commit, CUDA image, and the sole B200 PCP lane all passed without retry. TP2/PCP2 scored 0.9121, TP1/PCP4 scored 0.9454, and TP1/PCP4/DCP4 scored 0.8832; each completed all 1,319 questions with invalid rate 0.000. The exact job finished 3 passed in 17m54s.

AI assistance was used for investigation, current-main adaptation, CI configuration, and validation. No human review is claimed.
